def toggle_dark_mode_action():
    app_state = get_app_state()
    app_state.dark_mode = not app_state.dark_mode
    val = 'Dark' if app_state.dark_mode else 'Light'
    if fetch_one("SELECT id FROM app_config WHERE category = 'THEME_PREF'"):
        execute("UPDATE app_config SET value = ? WHERE category = 'THEME_PREF'", (val,))
    else:
        execute("INSERT INTO app_config (category, value, display_order) VALUES (?, ?, 0)", ('THEME_PREF', val))
    st.toast(f"Dark mode toggled to {val}!")
    st.rerun()

def get_option_menu_styles() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns the unified styling dictionary for streamlit_option_menu.option_menu
    that dynamically switches based on active theme and brand preferences."""
    app_state = get_app_state()
    is_dark = app_state.dark_mode
    brand_theme = getattr(app_state, "brand_theme", "oracle")
    mode = "dark" if is_dark else "light"
    
    cfg = THEME_CONFIGS.get(brand_theme, THEME_CONFIGS["oracle"])[mode]
    accent = cfg["menu_accent"]
    border = cfg["menu_border"]
    selected_text = cfg["menu_selected_text"]
        
    return {
        "container": {"padding": "0!important", "background-color": "transparent", "border": f"1px solid {border}"},
        "icon": {"font-size": "16px"}, 
        "nav-link": {"font-size": "16px", "text-align": "center", "margin": "0px"},
        "nav-link-selected": {"background-color": accent, "color": selected_text},
    }

def get_sub_option_menu_styles() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns the styling dictionary for nested sub-tabs (border-bottom selected tab design)
    that dynamically switches based on active theme and brand preferences."""
    app_state = get_app_state()
    is_dark = app_state.dark_mode
    brand_theme = getattr(app_state, "brand_theme", "oracle")
    mode = "dark" if is_dark else "light"
    
    cfg = THEME_CONFIGS.get(brand_theme, THEME_CONFIGS["oracle"])[mode]
    accent = cfg["sub_menu_accent"]
    bg = cfg["sub_menu_bg"]
        
    return {
        "container": {"padding": "0!important", "background-color": "transparent", "border": "none"},
        "icon": {"font-size": "14px"}, 
        "nav-link": {"font-size": "14px", "text-align": "center", "margin": "0px", "padding": "4px 8px"},
        "nav-link-selected": {"background-color": bg, "border-bottom": f"2px solid {accent}"},
    }

def get_main_command_palette_actions(current_org: str, current_prj: str, from_page: str = "/"):
    """Defines the available actions for the Command Palette dynamically."""
    app_state = get_app_state()
    dynamic_actions: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    user_id = app_state.user.current_user_id
    if user_id:
        recent_projects_df = query("""
            SELECT p.name as project_name, o.name as org_name
            FROM recent_projects rp
            JOIN projects p ON rp.project_id = p.id
            JOIN orgs o ON p.org_id = o.id
            WHERE rp.user_id = ? AND p.is_deleted = 0 AND o.is_deleted = 0
            ORDER BY rp.last_accessed DESC
            LIMIT 5
        """, (user_id,))

        for _, row in recent_projects_df.iterrows():
            action_name = f"Go to Project: {row['org_name']} - {row['project_name']}"
            dynamic_actions[action_name] = {
                "page": "pages/02_🔍_Project_Dashboard.py",
                "icon": "📂",
                "query_params": {"org": row['org_name'], "prj": row['project_name']}
            }

    all_actions = {
        "Go to National Dashboard": {"page": "pages/01_📊_Dashboard.py", "icon": "📊"},
        "Go to My Day": {"page": "pages/29_📅_My_Day.py", "icon": "📅"},
        "Go to Activity Feed": {"page": "pages/48_📰_Activity_Feed.py", "icon": "📰"},
        "Go to Project Dashboard": {"page": "pages/02_🔍_Project_Dashboard.py", "icon": "🔍"},
        "Go to Minutes Intelligence": {"page": "pages/03_📄_Minutes_Intelligence.py", "icon": "📄"},
        "Go to Email Log": {"page": "pages/04_📧_Email_Log.py", "icon": "📧"},
        "Go to Finance Dashboard": {"page": "pages/05_💰_Finance_Dashboard.py", "icon": "💰"},
        "Go to Task List": {"page": "pages/06_📋_Task_List.py", "icon": "📋"},
        "Go to Risk Log": {"page": "pages/07_⚠️_Risk_Log.py", "icon": "⚠️"},

def _on_dismiss_palette():
    st.session_state.pop("show_command_palette", None)
    st.session_state.pop("command_palette_from_page", None)

@st.dialog("Command Palette", on_dismiss=_on_dismiss_palette)
def _show_command_palette_dialog(current_org: str, current_prj: str, from_page: str):
    original_rerun = st.rerun
    def custom_rerun():
        st.session_state.pop("show_command_palette", None)
        st.session_state.pop("command_palette_from_page", None)
        original_rerun()
    st.rerun = custom_rerun

    try:
        actions = get_main_command_palette_actions(current_org, current_prj, from_page)
        
        search_term = st.text_input("Search actions...", key="command_palette_search", placeholder="Type an action or page name...", label_visibility="collapsed")
        
        filtered_actions = {
            k: v for k, v in actions.items()
            if search_term.lower() in k.lower()
        }
        filtered_actions = dict(sorted(filtered_actions.items()))

        if not filtered_actions:
            st.info("No matching actions found.")
        else:
            for action_name, action_info in filtered_actions.items():
                if st.button(f"{action_info['icon']} {action_name}", key=f"cmd_pal_{action_name}", use_container_width=True):
                    st.session_state.pop("show_command_palette", None)
                    st.session_state.pop("command_palette_from_page", None)
                    if "page" in action_info:
                        if "query_params" in action_info:
                            for k, v in action_info["query_params"].items():
                                st.query_params[k] = v
                        st.switch_page(action_info["page"])
                    elif "action_func" in action_info:
                        action_info["action_func"]()
                        st.rerun()

        app_state = get_app_state()
        if 'command_palette_download_data' in app_state.page_specific:
            st.download_button(
                label=f"Click to Download: {app_state.page_specific['command_palette_download_filename']}",
                data=app_state.page_specific.pop('command_palette_download_data'),
                file_name=app_state.page_specific.pop('command_palette_download_filename'),
                mime=app_state.page_specific.pop('command_palette_download_mime'),
                key="command_palette_final_download",
                use_container_width=True
            )
    finally:
        st.rerun = original_rerun

def render_pagination_controls(total_items: int, items_per_page: int, key: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Renders standardized, premium pagination controls."""
    if total_items <= 0:
        return 0, 0
        
    total_pages = max(1, math.ceil(total_items / items_per_page))
    
    state_key = f"paginator_page_{key}"
    if state_key not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[state_key] = 1
        
    if st.session_state[state_key] > total_pages:
        st.session_state[state_key] = total_pages
    if st.session_state[state_key] < 1:
        st.session_state[state_key] = 1
        
    current_page = st.session_state[state_key]
    cols = st.columns([1, 1, 3, 1, 1])
    
    with cols[0]:
        if st.button("⏮️ First", key=f"btn_first_{key}", disabled=(current_page == 1), use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state[state_key] = 1
            st.rerun()
            
    with cols[1]:
        if st.button("◀️ Prev", key=f"btn_prev_{key}", disabled=(current_page == 1), use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state[state_key] = current_page - 1
            st.rerun()
            
    with cols[2]:
        st.markdown(f"<div style='text-align: center; line-height: 2.2rem; font-weight: 600;'>Page {current_page} of {total_pages} (Total: {total_items})</div>", unsafe_allow_html=True)
        
    with cols[3]:
        if st.button("Next ▶️", key=f"btn_next_{key}", disabled=(current_page == total_pages), use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state[state_key] = current_page + 1
            st.rerun()
            
    with cols[4]:
        if st.button("Last ⏭️", key=f"btn_last_{key}", disabled=(current_page == total_pages), use_container_width=True):
            st.session_state[state_key] = total_pages
            st.rerun()
            
    start_idx = (current_page - 1) * items_per_page
    end_idx = min(start_idx + items_per_page, total_items)
    
    return start_idx, end_idx

def format_app_date(date_obj: Any) -> str:
    """Formats a date according to the globally stored preferred date format."""
    if not date_obj:
        return ""
    
    from datetime import datetime, date
    dt = None
    if isinstance(date_obj, (datetime, date)):
        dt = date_obj
    elif isinstance(date_obj, str):
        clean_str = date_obj.strip()
        if not clean_str:
            return ""
        for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%d", "%d/%m/%Y", "%d %b %Y", "%d %B %Y", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"):
            try:
                dt = datetime.strptime(clean_str, fmt).date()
                break
            except ValueError:
                continue
    
    if not dt:
        return str(date_obj)
        
    pref = "YYYY-MM-DD"
    if "preferred_date_format" in st.session_state:
        pref = st.session_state["preferred_date_format"]
    else:
        try:
            from core.state import get_app_state
            app_state = get_app_state()
            pref = getattr(app_state.user, "preferred_date_format", "YYYY-MM-DD")
        except Exception:
            pass
            
    if pref == "DD/MM/YYYY":
        return dt.strftime("%d/%m/%Y")
    elif pref == "DD MMM YYYY":
        return dt.strftime("%d %b %Y")
    else:
        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

def format_date_by_preference(date_val: Any) -> str:
    return format_app_date(date_val)

import time
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def performance_loader(label="Loading Dashboard Data..."):
    """A context manager that displays a visual skeleton layout while operations resolve."""
    placeholder = st.empty()
    
    with placeholder.container():
        st.markdown(
            """
            <style>
            @keyframes skeleton-pulse {
                0% { opacity: 0.6; }
                50% { opacity: 1.0; }
                100% { opacity: 0.6; }
            }
            .skeleton-box {
                animation: skeleton-pulse 1.5s infinite ease-in-out;
                background-color: #e2e8f0;
                border-radius: 6px;
            }
            .skeleton-card {
                background-color: #ffffff;
                border: 1px solid #e2e8f0;
                border-radius: 8px;
                padding: 16px;
                margin-bottom: 12px;
                animation: skeleton-pulse 1.5s infinite ease-in-out;
            }
            </style>
            """,
            unsafe_allow_html=True
        )
        
        st.markdown(f"#### ⏳ {label}")
        
        c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
        for col in (c1, c2, c3):
            with col:
                st.markdown(
                    """
                    <div class="skeleton-card">
                        <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 18px; width: 60%; margin-bottom: 12px; background-color: #cbd5e0;"></div>
                        <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 14px; width: 85%; margin-bottom: 8px;"></div>
                        <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 14px; width: 40%;"></div>
                    </div>
                    """,
                    unsafe_allow_html=True
                )
                
        st.markdown(
            """
            <div class="skeleton-card" style="animation: none;">
                <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 20px; width: 25%; margin-bottom: 16px; background-color: #cbd5e0;"></div>
                <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 12px; width: 100%; margin-bottom: 8px;"></div>
                <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 12px; width: 95%; margin-bottom: 8px;"></div>
                <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 12px; width: 98%; margin-bottom: 8px;"></div>
                <div class="skeleton-box" style="height: 12px; width: 50%;"></div>
            </div>
            """,
            unsafe_allow_html=True
        )
        
        progress_bar = st.progress(0)
        for pct in range(0, 101, 20):
            progress_bar.progress(pct)
            time.sleep(0.02)
            
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        placeholder.empty()

def performance_loader_decorator(label="Loading Dashboard Data..."):
    def decorator(func):
        from functools import wraps
        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            with performance_loader(label):
                return func(*args, **kwargs)
        return wrapper
    return decorator

def evaluate_layout_brightness(color: Any) -> float:
    """Evaluates the layout brightness level of a given color."""
    import re
    default_brightness = 128.0
    
    if not color:
        return default_brightness
        
    r, g, b = None, None, None
    
    if isinstance(color, (tuple, list)):
        if len(color) >= 3:
            try:
                r, g, b = float(color[0]), float(color[1]), float(color[2])
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                return default_brightness
        else:
            return default_brightness
            
    elif isinstance(color, str):
        color_str = color.strip().lower()
        
        named_colors = {
            "black": (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            "white": (255.0, 255.0, 255.0),
            "red": (255.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            "green": (0.0, 255.0, 0.0),
            "blue": (0.0, 0.0, 255.0),
            "yellow": (255.0, 255.0, 0.0),
            "cyan": (0.0, 255.0, 255.0),
            "magenta": (255.0, 0.0, 255.0),
            "silver": (192.0, 192.0, 192.0),
            "gray": (128.0, 128.0, 128.0),
            "grey": (128.0, 128.0, 128.0),
            "maroon": (128.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            "olive": (128.0, 128.0, 0.0),
            "purple": (128.0, 0.0, 128.0),
            "teal": (0.0, 128.0, 128.0),
            "navy": (0.0, 0.0, 128.0),
            "orange": (255.0, 165.0, 0.0),
            "transparent": (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        }
        
        if color_str in named_colors:
            r, g, b = named_colors[color_str]
        elif color_str.startswith("rgb") or color_str.startswith("rgba"):
            match = re.match(r"^rgba?\s*\(\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?:\s*,\s*[\d\.]+)?\s*\)$", color_str)
            if match:
                try:
                    r, g, b = float(match.group(1)), float(match.group(2)), float(match.group(3))
                except ValueError:
                    return default_brightness
            else:
                return default_brightness
        else:
            hex_str = color_str.lstrip("#")
            if len(hex_str) == 8:
                hex_str = hex_str[:6]
            elif len(hex_str) == 4:
                hex_str = hex_str[:3]
                
            if len(hex_str) == 3:
                try:
                    r = int(hex_str[0] * 2, 16)
                    g = int(hex_str[1] * 2, 16)
                    b = int(hex_str[2] * 2, 16)
                except ValueError:
                    return default_brightness
            elif len(hex_str) == 6:
                try:
                    r = int(hex_str[0:2], 16)
                    g = int(hex_str[2:4], 16)
                    b = int(hex_str[4:6], 16)
                except ValueError:
                    return default_brightness
            else:
                return default_brightness
    else:
        return default_brightness
        
    if r is None or g is None or b is None:
        return default_brightness
        
    brightness = 0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b
    return brightness

def get_contrast_text_color(bg_color: Any, dark_text: str = "#000000", light_text: str = "#ffffff", threshold: float = 128.0) -> str:
    """Returns the high-contrast text color based on layout brightness."""
    brightness = evaluate_layout_brightness(bg_color)
    if brightness >= threshold:
        return dark_text
    else:
        return light_text

def register_altair_theme():
    """Registers and enables the Oracle Redwood theme for all Altair charts."""
    try:
        import altair as alt
        
        def redwood_theme_config():
            app_state = get_app_state()
            is_dark = app_state.dark_mode
            
            bg_color = "transparent"
            text_color = "#fcfbfa" if is_dark else "#161513"
            grid_color = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)" if is_dark else "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06)"
            accent_color = "#d25427" if is_dark else "#c74616"
            
            # Palette matching Redwood earth and clay tones
            color_palette = [
                "#d25427", # Terracotta
                "#e28743", # Ochre
                "#eab676", # Sand
                "#76b5c5", # Soft Teal
                "#873e23", # Clay
                "#1e3d59", # Warm Charcoal
                "#3d405b"  # Deep Slate
            ]
            
            return {
                'config': {
                    'background': bg_color,
                    'view': {
                        'fill': bg_color,
                        'stroke': 'transparent'
                    },
                    'title': {
                        'color': text_color,
                        'subtitleColor': text_color,
                        'font': 'Inter, sans-serif',
                        'fontSize': 15,
                        'fontWeight': 'bold'
                    },
                    'axis': {
                        'domainColor': text_color,
                        'grid': True,
                        'gridColor': grid_color,
                        'labelColor': text_color,
                        'tickColor': text_color,
                        'titleColor': text_color,
                        'labelFont': 'Inter, sans-serif',
                        'titleFont': 'Inter, sans-serif',
                        'labelFontSize': 11,
                        'titleFontSize': 13
                    },
                    'legend': {
                        'labelColor': text_color,
                        'titleColor': text_color,
                        'labelFont': 'Inter, sans-serif',
                        'titleFont': 'Inter, sans-serif',
                        'labelFontSize': 11,
                        'titleFontSize': 13
                    },
                    'range': {
                        'category': color_palette,
                        'diverging': ['#d4351c', '#ffdd00', '#00703c'], # RAG
                        'heatmap': ['#1c1a18', '#d25427'] if is_dark else ['#ffffff', '#c74616']
                    },
                    'mark': {
                        'color': accent_color
                    },
                    'bar': {
                        'fill': accent_color
                    },
                    'line': {
                        'stroke': accent_color
                    }
                }
            }
            
        alt.themes.register('redwood', redwood_theme_config)
        alt.themes.enable('redwood')
    except Exception:
        pass

# constants.py
import streamlit as st

# --- App Branding ---
# Toggle between display names. The active name is stored in app_config
# under category 'APP_BRANDING_MODE' with value 'people_portal' or 'fnws'.
APP_NAME_PEOPLE_PORTAL = "People Portal Programme"
APP_NAME_FNWS = "Future NHS Workforce Solution"

def get_app_display_name() -> str:
    """Returns the current application display name based on the branding toggle.
    Reads from session state (cached from app_config at login)."""
    mode = st.session_state.get("app_branding_mode", "fnws")
    if mode == "people_portal":
        return APP_NAME_PEOPLE_PORTAL
    return APP_NAME_FNWS

# auth_utils.py
import streamlit as st
from typing import Any, Tuple
from core.database_utils import fetch_one, query
from core.state import get_app_state
import bcrypt
from typing import List

# --- Role Definitions ---
# These roles are based on the user request for more granular permissions.
# They are mapped from the roles stored in the 'rit_team' table.
ADMIN_ROLES = ["National Director", "Admin", "Programme Director"]
PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLES = ["Implementation Manager (IM)"]
TEAM_MEMBER_ROLES = ["Implementation Advisor (IA)"]
STAKEHOLDER_ROLES = ["Strategic Implementation Lead (SIL)", "Implementation Lead (IL)"]

# --- Password Hashing Context ---
def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    """Hashes a password using bcrypt."""
    # Truncate password to 72 bytes for bcrypt compatibility
    password_bytes = password[:72].encode('utf-8')
    salt = bcrypt.gensalt()
    hashed_bytes = bcrypt.hashpw(password_bytes, salt)
    return hashed_bytes.decode('utf-8')

def verify_password(plain_password: str, hashed_password: str) -> bool:
    """Verifies a plain password against a bcrypt hash."""
    # Truncate password to 72 bytes for bcrypt compatibility
    plain_password_bytes = plain_password[:72].encode('utf-8')
    hashed_password_bytes = hashed_password.encode('utf-8')
    return bcrypt.checkpw(plain_password_bytes, hashed_password_bytes)

@st.cache_data(ttl=60)
def user_has_permission(role: str, action: str) -> bool:
    """
    Checks the database to see if a role has permission for a specific action.
    Caches the result for 60 seconds to reduce database lookups.
    """
    # 1. Check for admin wildcard first (highest priority)
    if fetch_one("SELECT id FROM permissions WHERE role = ? AND action = '*'", (role,)):
        return True
    
    # 2. Check for the specific permission
    res = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM permissions WHERE role = ? AND action = ?", (role, action))
    return res is not None

@st.cache_data(ttl=300)
def _get_project_im_leads(project_id: int) -> List[str]:
    project_org_id_row = fetch_one("SELECT org_id FROM projects WHERE id = ?", (project_id,))
    if project_org_id_row:
        org_id = project_org_id_row[0]
        org_region_row = fetch_one("SELECT region FROM orgs WHERE id = ?", (org_id,))
        if org_region_row:
            region = org_region_row[0]
            im_leads_df = query("SELECT im_lead FROM region_mapping WHERE sub_region = ?", (region,))
            if not im_leads_df.empty:
                return [name.strip() for name in str(im_leads_df.iloc[0]['im_lead']).split(',') if name.strip()]
    return []

def user_can(action: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """
    Central function to check user permissions for a given action.
    This provides a single point of truth for all authorization logic.
    Returns a tuple: (has_permission: bool, reason: str).

    Usage:
    can_edit, reason = user_can("edit_risk", owner=risk_owner)
    if not can_edit:
        st.warning(reason)
    """
    app_state = get_app_state()
    user_id = app_state.user.current_user_id
    user_name = app_state.user.current_user

    # --- FIX: Combine primary and additional roles for a complete permission set ---
    primary_role = app_state.user.current_user_role
    additional_roles = app_state.user.current_user_roles
    user_roles = set(additional_roles)
    if primary_role:
        user_roles.add(primary_role)

    if not user_roles or not user_name:
        return False, "Access Denied: User not logged in or has no assigned roles."

    # --- NEW: Bootstrap Admin ---
    # If the user is the first user in the system (ID 1), grant them all permissions.
    # This prevents being locked out of the system on a fresh install.
    if user_id == 1:
        return True, ""

    # 1. Check for Super Admin first (wildcard '*' permission in the database).
    # This is the highest privilege and covers any role with full access.
    is_super_admin = any(user_has_permission(role, '*') for role in user_roles)
    if is_super_admin:
        return True, ""

    # 2. If not a super admin, check for the specific permission.
    has_base_permission = any(user_has_permission(role, action) for role in user_roles)
    if not has_base_permission:
        return False, f"Access Denied: Your role(s) do not have permission to perform the action '{action}'."

    # 3. If they have the permission, apply context-specific checks.
    if action in ["edit_action", "edit_risk"]:
        owner = kwargs.get("owner")
        project_id = kwargs.get("project_id")

        # Check 1: Is the user the assigned owner?
        if owner == user_name:
            return True, ""

        # Check 2: Is the user a Project Manager (IM) for this project's region?
        is_im = any(role == "Implementation Manager (IM)" for role in user_roles)
        if is_im and project_id:
            im_leads_for_region = _get_project_im_leads(project_id)
            if user_name in im_leads_for_region:
                return True, ""

        # If neither owner nor authorized IM, deny access
        return False, "Access Denied: You must be the owner of this item or a Project Manager for this project's region to perform this action."

    # If the action has a base permission but no specific contextual checks, grant access.
    return True, ""

# --- NEW: Permissions for Lessons Learned ---
# These will be seeded in patch_database in database_utils.py

def process_overdue_task_alerts():
    """Finds overdue tasks and creates notifications based on user preferences."""
    logger.info("⏰ Running automated overdue task alerts...")
    
    # 1. Fetch SMTP Config using the new get_secret helper
    from core.database_utils import get_secret
    smtp_server = get_secret("SMTP_SERVER")
    smtp_port = get_secret("SMTP_PORT")
    smtp_user = get_secret("SMTP_USER")
    smtp_pass = get_secret("SMTP_PASS")

    can_email = all([smtp_server, smtp_port, smtp_user, smtp_pass])
    if not can_email:
        logger.warning("SMTP not fully configured. Skipping email notifications.")

    today = datetime.now().date()
    sql = """
        SELECT a.task, a.assigned_to, a.due_date, p.name as Stream, o.name as Trust
        FROM actions a
        JOIN projects p ON a.project_id = p.id
        JOIN orgs o ON p.org_id = o.id
        WHERE a.status != 'Closed' AND a.is_deleted = 0 AND p.is_deleted = 0 AND o.is_deleted = 0
        AND a.due_date < ?
    """
    overdue_df = query(sql, (str(today),))
    
    if overdue_df.empty:
        logger.info("No overdue tasks found. The team is on track!")
        return
        
    # 2. Get user preferences for this event type
    prefs_df = query("SELECT user_name FROM notification_prefs WHERE event_type = 'TASK_OVERDUE' AND is_active = 1")
    subscribed_users = prefs_df['user_name'].tolist()

    # 3. Group tasks by owner and create notifications
    for owner, tasks in overdue_df.groupby('assigned_to'):
        if not owner or pd.isna(owner) or owner not in subscribed_users:
            continue

        # Create In-App Notification
        message = f"You have {len(tasks)} overdue tasks requiring attention."
        link = "pages/06_📋_Task_List.py"
        # Avoid creating duplicate notifications if the job runs frequently
        last_notif = fetch_one("SELECT timestamp FROM notifications WHERE user_name = ? AND message = ? ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1", (owner, message))
        if last_notif:
            last_notif_time = datetime.strptime(last_notif[0], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
            if (datetime.now() - last_notif_time) < timedelta(days=1):
                continue # Skip if a similar notification was sent in the last 24 hours

        execute("INSERT INTO notifications (user_name, message, link, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (owner, message, link, datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")))
        logger.info(f"Generated in-app overdue task notification for {owner}")

        # Send Email Notification (if configured)
        if can_email:
            # We know these are not None because of the `all()` check above.
            # The type ignore is to satisfy the type checker which can't infer this.

            try:
                with smtplib.SMTP(str(smtp_server), int(smtp_port)) as server: # type: ignore
                    server.starttls()
                    server.login(str(smtp_user), str(smtp_pass)) # type: ignore
                    
                    task_list_str = ""
                    for _, r in tasks.iterrows():
                        task_list_str += f"- {r['task']} (Due: {r['due_date']}) [{r['Trust']} / {r['Stream']}]\n"
                    
                    msg = EmailMessage()
                    msg.set_content(f"Hi {owner},\n\nYou have {len(tasks)} overdue tasks requiring an update:\n\n{task_list_str}\n\nPlease log into the People Portal Programme to update these as soon as possible.\n\nThanks,\nProgramme Management AI")
                    msg['Subject'] = f"Overdue Tasks Alert ({len(tasks)} Tasks)"
                    msg['From'] = str(smtp_user)
                    msg['To'] = str(owner).replace(" ", ".").lower() + "@nhs.net"
                    server.send_message(msg)
                    logger.info(f"✅ Sent automated email to {owner}")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Failed to send email to {owner}: {e}")

def process_recurring_tasks():
    """Checks for and creates new instances of recurring tasks."""
    logger.info("🔄 Checking for recurring tasks...")
    today = datetime.now().date()
    
    sql = """
        SELECT id, project_id, task, assigned_to, recurring_frequency, next_occurrence_date
        FROM actions
        WHERE is_recurring = 1 AND original_task_id IS NULL
        AND next_occurrence_date <= ?
    """
    tasks_to_recreate = query(sql, (str(today),))
    
    if tasks_to_recreate.empty:
        logger.info("No recurring tasks to generate today.")
        return
        
    for _, task in tasks_to_recreate.iterrows():
        try:
            new_task_due_date = datetime.strptime(task['next_occurrence_date'], "%Y-%m-%d").date()
            
            if task['recurring_frequency'] == 'Daily':
                next_occurrence = new_task_due_date + timedelta(days=1)
            elif task['recurring_frequency'] == 'Weekly':
                next_occurrence = new_task_due_date + timedelta(weeks=1)
            elif task['recurring_frequency'] == 'Monthly':
                next_occurrence = new_task_due_date + timedelta(days=30) # Simplification
            else:
                execute("UPDATE actions SET is_recurring = 0 WHERE id = ?", (task['id'],))
                continue

            new_task_start_date = new_task_due_date - timedelta(days=3)
            
            execute("""
                INSERT INTO actions (project_id, task, assigned_to, start_date, due_date, status, original_task_id)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """, (task['project_id'], task['task'], task['assigned_to'], str(new_task_start_date), str(new_task_due_date), 'Open', task['id']))
            
            execute("UPDATE actions SET next_occurrence_date = ? WHERE id = ?", (str(next_occurrence), task['id']))
            logger.info(f"✅ Generated new recurring task for '{task['task']}' due {str(new_task_due_date)}.")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to process recurring task ID {task['id']}: {e}")

def process_upcoming_task_alerts():
    """Finds tasks due soon (in 3 days) and creates notifications."""
    logger.info("⏰ Running upcoming task deadline alerts...")
    
    three_days_from_now = (datetime.now() + timedelta(days=3)).date()
    
    sql = """
        SELECT a.task, a.assigned_to, a.due_date
        FROM actions a
        WHERE a.status != 'Closed' AND a.is_deleted = 0
        AND a.due_date = ?
    """
    upcoming_df = query(sql, (str(three_days_from_now),))
    
    if upcoming_df.empty:
        logger.info("No tasks due in 3 days.")
        return
        
    for owner, tasks in upcoming_df.groupby('assigned_to'):
        if not owner or pd.isna(owner):
            continue

        message = f"You have {len(tasks)} task(s) due in 3 days."
        create_notifications_for_event(event_type='TASK_UPCOMING', message=message, link="pages/06_📋_Task_List.py", direct_user=owner)
        logger.info(f"Generated upcoming task notification for {owner}")

def process_kpi_breach_alerts():
    """Finds tasks that are overdue beyond the configured KPI window and creates alerts."""
    logger.info("🎯 Running KPI breach alerts...")
    from core.database_utils import get_secret
    
    kpi_days_str = get_secret("TASK_BREACH_KPI_DAYS")
    if not kpi_days_str:
        logger.info("KPI breach check skipped: No threshold set in configuration.")
        return
    
    kpi_days = int(kpi_days_str)
    breach_date = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=kpi_days)).date()

    # Find tasks that are overdue beyond the KPI window and haven't been notified yet
    breached_tasks_df = query("""
        SELECT a.id, a.task, a.assigned_to, p.id as project_id, p.name as project_name
        FROM actions a
        JOIN projects p ON a.project_id = p.id
        WHERE a.status != 'Closed' AND a.is_deleted = 0 AND a.kpi_breach_notified = 0
        AND a.due_date < ?
    """, (str(breach_date),))

    if breached_tasks_df.empty:
        logger.info("No new KPI breaches found.")
        return

    for _, task in breached_tasks_df.iterrows():
        task_id = task['id']
        task_desc = task['task']
        owner = task['assigned_to']
        project_id = task['project_id']
        project_name = task['project_name']

        # 1. Create a notification for the owner
        if owner:
            message = f"KPI Breach on '{project_name}': Task '{task_desc[:30]}...' is over {kpi_days} days overdue."
            create_notifications_for_event(
                event_type='KPI_BREACH', 
                project_id=project_id, 
                message=message, 
                link=f"pages/06_📋_Task_List.py",
                direct_user=owner
            )
        execute("UPDATE actions SET kpi_breach_notified = 1 WHERE id = ?", (task_id,))
        logger.info(f"Processed KPI breach for task ID {task_id}.")

def process_scheduled_reports():
    """Finds and runs scheduled reports, emailing the PDF.
    
    Opens a single SMTP session for all reports to avoid repeated
    TLS handshakes and authentication round-trips per report.
    """
    logger.info("📅 Running scheduled report generation...")
    
    from core.database_utils import get_secret
    smtp_server = get_secret("SMTP_SERVER")
    smtp_port = get_secret("SMTP_PORT")
    smtp_user = get_secret("SMTP_USER")
    smtp_pass = get_secret("SMTP_PASS")
    
    can_email = all([smtp_server, smtp_port, smtp_user, smtp_pass])
    if not can_email:
        logger.warning("SMTP not configured. Skipping scheduled report emails.")
        return

    today = datetime.now()
    due_reports_df = query("SELECT * FROM scheduled_reports WHERE is_active = 1 AND is_deleted = 0")
    
    # Collect reports that are due to run today
    due_rows = []
    for _, report_row in due_reports_df.iterrows():
        should_run = False
        if report_row['frequency'] == 'Daily':
            should_run = True
        elif report_row['frequency'] == 'Weekly' and today.weekday() == 0:
            should_run = True
        elif report_row['frequency'] == 'Monthly' and today.day == 1:
            should_run = True
        if should_run:
            due_rows.append(report_row)

    if not due_rows:
        logger.info("No scheduled reports due today.")
        return

    # Open a single SMTP connection for all reports
    try:
        smtp_conn = smtplib.SMTP(str(smtp_server), int(smtp_port))  # type: ignore
        smtp_conn.starttls()
        smtp_conn.login(str(smtp_user), str(smtp_pass))  # type: ignore
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to connect to SMTP for scheduled reports: {e}")
        return

    try:
        for report_row in due_rows:
            logger.info(f"Generating scheduled report: {report_row['report_name']}")
            try:
                config = json.loads(report_row['report_config'])
                df_report, chart, report_title = generate_report_from_config(config)

                pdf = ReportPDF(title=report_title)
                pdf.add_page()
                pdf.chapter_title(report_title)
                pdf.chapter_body(f"Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}")
                
                if not df_report.empty:
                    col_widths = []
                    page_width = pdf.w - 2 * pdf.l_margin
                    num_cols = len(df_report.columns)
                    if num_cols > 0:
                        col_width = page_width / num_cols
                        col_widths = [col_width] * num_cols
                    pdf.add_df_to_pdf(df_report, col_widths=col_widths)

                if chart is not None:
                    pdf.add_page()
                    pdf.chapter_title(f"{report_row['report_name']} Visualization")
                    chart_png_bytes = vlc.vegalite_to_png(chart.to_dict())
                    image_stream = io.BytesIO(chart_png_bytes)
                    pdf.image(image_stream, x=pdf.l_margin, w=page_width)

                pdf_bytes = bytes(pdf.output())

                recipients = [r.strip() for r in report_row['recipients'].split(',') if r.strip()]
                if recipients:
                    msg = EmailMessage()
                    msg['Subject'] = f"Scheduled Report: {report_row['report_name']}"
                    msg['From'] = str(smtp_user)
                    msg['To'] = ', '.join(recipients)
                    msg.set_content(f"Please find your scheduled report '{report_row['report_name']}' attached.")
                    msg.add_attachment(pdf_bytes, maintype='application', subtype='pdf', filename=f"{report_row['report_name'].replace(' ', '_')}.pdf")
                    smtp_conn.send_message(msg)
                    logger.info(f"✅ Sent scheduled report '{report_row['report_name']}' to {recipients}")
                execute("UPDATE scheduled_reports SET last_run_date = ? WHERE id = ?", (today.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), report_row['id']))

            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Failed to generate/send scheduled report ID {report_row['id']}: {e}")
    finally:
        smtp_conn.quit()

def run_proactive_ai_insights():
    """
    Runs AI-driven proactive insights for active projects.
    
    Circuit breaker: caps at MAX_PROJECTS_PER_AI_RUN per run, prioritising
    Red RAG projects first so the most critical work is always analysed.
    Projects are also skipped if they were analysed in the last 24 hours to
    prevent redundant LLM calls during frequent scheduler restarts.
    """
    MAX_PROJECTS_PER_AI_RUN = 15
    logger.info(f"🧠 Running proactive AI insights (max {MAX_PROJECTS_PER_AI_RUN} projects per run)...")
    from core.ai_utils import predict_risk_trends, identify_task_bottlenecks, predict_budget_overrun, predict_resource_conflicts, detect_sentiment_shifts
    
    # Order by RAG status: Red first, then Amber, then Green. Limit to circuit-breaker cap.
    projects_df = query(
        """SELECT id, name, start_date, due_date, rag_status
           FROM projects
           WHERE is_deleted = 0 AND status NOT IN ('Complete', 'Withdrawn')
           ORDER BY CASE rag_status WHEN 'Red' THEN 0 WHEN 'Amber' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END
           LIMIT ?""",
        (MAX_PROJECTS_PER_AI_RUN,)
    )
    if projects_df.empty:
        logger.info("No active projects to analyze for proactive insights.")
        return

    for _, project in projects_df.iterrows():
        project_id = project['id']
        project_name = project['name']

        # --- Risk Trend Prediction ---
        df_risks = query("SELECT impact, description, mitigation, status FROM risks WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10", (project_id,))
        df_meetings = query("SELECT summary, thematic FROM meetings WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0 ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 5", (project_id,))
        
        risk_context = f"Recent Risks:\n{df_risks.to_string(index=False)}\n\nRecent Meeting Discussions:\n{df_meetings.to_string(index=False)}"
        try:
            risk_insights = predict_risk_trends(risk_context)
            if "no significant risk trends" not in risk_insights.lower():
                message = f"AI identified potential risk trends for '{project_name}':\n{risk_insights}"
                create_notifications_for_event(event_type='AI_PROACTIVE_RISK', project_id=project_id, message=message, link="pages/02_🔍_Project_Dashboard.py")
                logger.info(f"AI generated risk insights for project {project_id}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"AI Risk Trend Prediction failed for project {project_id}: {e}")

        # --- Task Bottleneck Identification ---
        df_tasks = query("SELECT task, assigned_to, start_date, due_date, status, depends_on_id FROM actions WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0 AND status != 'Closed' ORDER BY due_date ASC LIMIT 20", (project_id,))
        task_context = f"Open Tasks:\n{df_tasks.to_string(index=False)}"
        try:
            task_insights = identify_task_bottlenecks(task_context)
            if "no significant task bottlenecks" not in task_insights.lower():
                message = f"AI identified potential task bottlenecks for '{project_name}':\n{task_insights}"
                create_notifications_for_event(event_type='AI_PROACTIVE_TASK', project_id=project_id, message=message, link="pages/02_🔍_Project_Dashboard.py")
                logger.info(f"AI generated task insights for project {project_id}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"AI Task Bottleneck Identification failed for project {project_id}: {e}")

        # --- NEW: Budget Overrun Prediction ---
        df_budgets = query("SELECT budget_name, total_budget FROM budgets WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", (project_id,))
        df_expenses = query("SELECT SUM(amount) as total_spent, COUNT(*) as num_expenses FROM expenses WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", (project_id,))
        
        total_budget = df_budgets['total_budget'].sum()
        total_spent = df_expenses['total_spent'].iloc[0] if not df_expenses.empty and pd.notna(df_expenses['total_spent'].iloc[0]) else 0
        
        if total_budget > 0:
            budget_context = f"""
            Project Start Date: {project.get('start_date')}
            Project Target End Date: {project.get('due_date')}
            Total Budget: {total_budget:,.2f}
            Total Spent to Date: {total_spent:,.2f}
            Number of Expense Items: {df_expenses['num_expenses'].iloc[0] if not df_expenses.empty else 0}
            """
            try:
                budget_insights = predict_budget_overrun(budget_context)
                if "no significant" not in budget_insights.lower():
                    message = f"AI identified a potential budget risk for '{project_name}':\n{budget_insights}"
                    create_notifications_for_event(event_type='AI_PROACTIVE_BUDGET', project_id=project_id, message=message, link="pages/05_💰_Finance_Dashboard.py")
                    logger.info(f"AI generated budget insights for project {project_id}")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"AI Budget Overrun Prediction failed for project {project_id}: {e}")

        # --- NEW: Resource Conflict Prediction ---
        twelve_weeks_from_now = (datetime.now() + timedelta(weeks=12)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        df_allocations = query("""
            SELECT rt.name, ra.allocation_pct, ra.start_date, ra.end_date
            FROM resource_allocations ra
            JOIN rit_team rt ON ra.user_id = rt.id
            WHERE ra.project_id = ? AND ra.is_deleted = 0
            AND (ra.end_date IS NULL OR ra.end_date >= date('now'))
        """, (project_id,))
        df_critical_tasks = query("SELECT task, assigned_to, due_date FROM actions WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0 AND status != 'Closed' AND rag_status = 'Red' AND due_date <= ?", (project_id, twelve_weeks_from_now))

        if not df_allocations.empty:
            resource_context = f"Current & Future Resource Allocations:\n{df_allocations.to_string(index=False)}\n\nUpcoming Critical Tasks (next 12 weeks):\n{df_critical_tasks.to_string(index=False)}"
            try:
                resource_insights = predict_resource_conflicts(resource_context)
                if "no significant" not in resource_insights.lower():
                    message = f"AI identified a potential resource conflict for '{project_name}':\n{resource_insights}"
                    create_notifications_for_event(event_type='AI_PROACTIVE_RESOURCE', project_id=project_id, message=message, link="pages/09_👥_Resource_Planner.py")
                    logger.info(f"AI generated resource insights for project {project_id}")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"AI Resource Conflict Prediction failed for project {project_id}: {e}")

        # --- NEW: Sentiment Shift Detection ---
        three_months_ago = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=90)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
        df_sentiment_emails = query("SELECT date_sent as date, sentiment_score FROM emails WHERE project_id = ? AND sentiment_score IS NOT NULL AND is_deleted = 0 AND date_sent >= ?", (project_id, three_months_ago))
        df_sentiment_meetings = query("SELECT date, sentiment_score FROM meetings WHERE project_id = ? AND sentiment_score IS NOT NULL AND is_deleted = 0 AND date >= ?", (project_id, three_months_ago))
        df_sentiment = pd.concat([df_sentiment_emails, df_sentiment_meetings]).sort_values(by='date').reset_index(drop=True)
        
        if len(df_sentiment) > 3:
            sentiment_context = f"Recent Sentiment Scores (Date, Score):\n{df_sentiment.to_string(index=False)}"
            try:
                sentiment_insights = detect_sentiment_shifts(sentiment_context)
                if "no significant" not in sentiment_insights.lower():
                    message = f"AI detected a negative sentiment shift for '{project_name}':\n{sentiment_insights}"
                    create_notifications_for_event(event_type='AI_PROACTIVE_SENTIMENT', project_id=project_id, message=message, link="pages/04_📧_Email_Log.py")
                    logger.info(f"AI generated sentiment insights for project {project_id}")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"AI Sentiment Shift Detection failed for project {project_id}: {e}")

def run_ai_agent_assignments():
    """
    Proactive AI agent that finds unassigned critical risks and suggests an owner.
    """
    logger.info("🤖 Running AI Agent for critical risk assignments...")
    
    unassigned_risks_df = query("""
        SELECT r.id, r.description, r.project_id, p.name as project_name, o.region 
        FROM risks r 
        JOIN projects p ON r.project_id = p.id 
        JOIN orgs o ON p.org_id = o.id 
        WHERE r.impact = 'Critical' AND r.status = 'Open' AND (r.owner IS NULL OR r.owner = '') AND r.is_deleted = 0
    """)

    if unassigned_risks_df.empty:
        logger.info("AI Agent: No unassigned critical risks found.")
        return

    # Get all IA workloads once for efficiency
    from core.logic import get_all_ia_workload_scores, get_leadership_team, suggest_best_ia
    from core.ai_utils import extract_skill_from_risk
    all_workloads = get_all_ia_workload_scores()

    for _, risk in unassigned_risks_df.iterrows():
        try:
            risk_id = risk['id']
            risk_desc = risk['description']
            project_id = risk['project_id']
            project_name = risk['project_name']
            region = risk['region']

            # 1. Find the Project Manager (IM) for this project's region
            leadership = get_leadership_team(region)
            if not leadership or not leadership.get('IM') or leadership['IM'] == "Unassigned":
                logger.warning(f"AI Agent: Could not find an IM for region '{region}' to notify for risk {risk_id}.")
                continue
            
            project_manager_name = leadership['IM'].split(',')[0].strip() # Take the first one if multiple
            strategic_area = leadership.get('Area')

            if not strategic_area:
                logger.warning(f"AI Agent: Could not find a strategic area for region '{region}' for risk {risk_id}.")
                continue

            # 2. Use AI to determine the required skill
            required_skill = extract_skill_from_risk(risk_desc)
            
            # 3. Suggest the best IA
            suggested_owner_str = suggest_best_ia(strategic_area, all_workloads, required_skill)
            
            # Parse the suggested owner name (it might include workload info)
            suggested_owner_match = re.match(r"^(.*?)\s*\(", suggested_owner_str)
            suggested_owner = suggested_owner_match.group(1).strip() if suggested_owner_match else suggested_owner_str

            if "No IA mapped" in suggested_owner:
                logger.info(f"AI Agent: No suitable IA found for risk {risk_id} in area '{strategic_area}'.")
                continue

            # 4. Create a notification for the PM with a one-click approval link
            encoded_owner = urllib.parse.quote(suggested_owner)
            approval_link = f"pages/07_⚠️_Risk_Log.py?action=assign_risk&risk_id={risk_id}&owner={encoded_owner}"
            
            message = f"AI Agent suggests assigning critical risk on '{project_name}' to **{suggested_owner}**. Risk: '{risk_desc[:40]}...'. Click to approve."
            
            create_notifications_for_event(
                event_type='AI_SUGGESTED_ASSIGNMENT',
                message=message,
                link=approval_link,
                project_id=project_id,
                direct_user=project_manager_name
            )
            logger.info(f"AI Agent: Sent assignment suggestion for risk {risk_id} to PM {project_manager_name}.")

        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"AI Agent failed to process risk {risk.get('id', 'N/A')}: {e}")

def run_compliance_checks():
    """
    Executes all active compliance rules, logs violations, and updates rule status.
    """
    logger.info("🛡️ Running automated compliance checks...")
    
    active_rules = query("SELECT id, rule_name, rule_type, rule_definition, severity FROM compliance_rules WHERE is_active = 1 AND is_deleted = 0")
    
    if active_rules.empty:
        logger.info("No active compliance rules to check.")
        return

    for _, rule in active_rules.iterrows():
        rule_id = rule['id']
        rule_name = rule['rule_name']
        rule_type = rule['rule_type']
        rule_definition = rule['rule_definition']
        severity = rule['severity']
        
        logger.info(f"Checking rule: {rule_name} (ID: {rule_id})")
        
        violations_found = 0
        last_result_summary = {"status": "No violations", "count": 0}
        
        try:
            if rule_type == 'SQL_QUERY':
                # Execute the SQL query defined in the rule
                violation_df = query(rule_definition)
                
                if not violation_df.empty:
                    violations_found = len(violation_df)
                    last_result_summary["status"] = f"{violations_found} violations found"
                    last_result_summary["count"] = violations_found

                    for _, violation_row in violation_df.iterrows():
                        # Attempt to extract project_id and entity_id from the violation row
                        # The SQL query should ideally return these for better logging
                        project_id = violation_row.get('project_id')
                        entity_id = violation_row.get('id') # Assuming 'id' is the entity ID
                        
                        # Log each violation
                        execute(
                            "INSERT INTO compliance_violations (rule_id, project_id, entity_id, violation_details, timestamp, is_resolved) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                            (rule_id, project_id, entity_id, json.dumps(violation_row.to_dict()), datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), 0)
                        )
                        
                        # Create a notification for high severity violations
                        if severity == 'High':
                            message = f"Compliance Violation: '{rule_name}' - {violation_row.get('description', 'Details in Compliance Dashboard')}"
                            create_notifications_for_event(
                                event_type='COMPLIANCE_VIOLATION',
                                project_id=project_id,
                                message=message,
                                link="pages/10_🛡️_Compliance_Dashboard.py"
                            )
            else:
                last_result_summary["status"] = f"Error: Unsupported rule type '{rule_type}'"
                logger.error(f"Unsupported rule type for rule {rule_id}: {rule_type}")

        except Exception as e:
            last_result_summary["status"] = f"Error during check: {str(e)}"
            logger.error(f"Error checking compliance rule {rule_id} ('{rule_name}'): {e}")
        finally:
            # Update the rule's last checked time and result summary
            execute(
                "UPDATE compliance_rules SET last_checked = ?, last_result = ? WHERE id = ?",
                (datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), json.dumps(last_result_summary), rule_id)
            )

def process_notification_digests():
    """Finds users with unread notifications and sends them a summary email digest.
    
    Uses a single shared SMTP connection for all users to avoid repeated
    TCP handshakes and SMTP authentication round-trips.
    """
    logger.info("📧 Running automated notification email digest...")

    from core.database_utils import get_secret
    smtp_server = get_secret("SMTP_SERVER")
    smtp_port = get_secret("SMTP_PORT")
    smtp_user = get_secret("SMTP_USER")
    smtp_pass = get_secret("SMTP_PASS")
    
    can_email = all([smtp_server, smtp_port, smtp_user, smtp_pass])
    if not can_email:
        logger.warning("SMTP not fully configured. Skipping email notification digests.")
        return

    sql = """
        SELECT user_name, message, timestamp, link
        FROM notifications
        WHERE is_read = 0
        ORDER BY user_name, timestamp DESC
    """
    unread_notifications_df = query(sql)

    if unread_notifications_df.empty:
        logger.info("No unread notifications to digest. All users are up to date!")
        return

    # Open a single SMTP connection and loop all users inside it
    try:
        with smtplib.SMTP(str(smtp_server), int(smtp_port)) as server:  # type: ignore
            server.starttls()
            server.login(str(smtp_user), str(smtp_pass))  # type: ignore
            for user, notifications in unread_notifications_df.groupby('user_name'):
                if not user or pd.isna(user):
                    continue
                try:
                    notification_list_str = ""
                    for _, notif in notifications.iterrows():
                        notification_list_str += f"- {notif['message']} (Received: {notif['timestamp']})\n"

                    msg = EmailMessage()
                    msg.set_content(f"Hi {user},\n\nYou have {len(notifications)} unread notifications in the People Portal Programme:\n\n{notification_list_str}\n\nPlease log in to view more details and take action.\n\nThanks,\nProgramme Management AI")
                    msg['Subject'] = f"Unread Notification Digest ({len(notifications)} items)"
                    msg['From'] = str(smtp_user)
                    msg['To'] = str(user).replace(" ", ".").lower() + "@nhs.net"
                    server.send_message(msg)
                    logger.info(f"✅ Sent notification digest email to {user}")
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.error(f"Failed to send notification digest to {user}: {e}")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Failed to connect to SMTP for notification digest: {e}")

import threading

_scheduler = None
_scheduler_lock = threading.Lock()

def init_scheduler():
    """Initializes the background scheduler exactly once (Singleton pattern)."""
    if os.environ.get("DISABLE_IN_PROCESS_SCHEDULER") == "1":
        logger.info("In-process scheduler disabled via DISABLE_IN_PROCESS_SCHEDULER=1. Skipping initialization.")
        return None
    global _scheduler
    with _scheduler_lock:
        if _scheduler is not None and _scheduler.running:
            logger.info("Scheduler already running. Skipping initialization.")
            return _scheduler

        _scheduler = BackgroundScheduler()
        # Schedule job to run every Monday at 8:00 AM
        _scheduler.add_job(process_overdue_task_alerts, 'cron', day_of_week='mon', hour=8, minute=0)  # type: ignore
        
        # Schedule job to run daily to generate reports
        _scheduler.add_job(process_scheduled_reports, 'cron', hour=7, minute=0) # Run daily at 7 AM
        # Schedule AI proactive insights to run daily
        _scheduler.add_job(run_proactive_ai_insights, 'cron', hour=3, minute=0) # Run daily at 3 AM

        # --- Seeding notification prefs (guarded to avoid repeated cache-clearing execute() calls) ---
        prefs_check = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM notification_prefs WHERE user_name = 'System' LIMIT 1")
        if not prefs_check:
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'AI_PROACTIVE_RISK')
            )
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'AI_PROACTIVE_TASK')
            )
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'AI_PROACTIVE_BUDGET')
            )
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'AI_PROACTIVE_RESOURCE')
            )
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'AI_PROACTIVE_SENTIMENT')
            )
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'AI_SUGGESTED_ASSIGNMENT')
            )
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'KPI_BREACH')
            )
            logger.info("Seeded default notification preferences for System.")

        # Ensure RED_FLAG_ANOMALY notification preferences are seeded
        anomaly_prefs_check = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM notification_prefs WHERE event_type = 'RED_FLAG_ANOMALY' LIMIT 1")
        if not anomaly_prefs_check:
            execute_silent(
                "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, ?, 1)",
                ('System', 'RED_FLAG_ANOMALY')
            )
            try:
                team_members_df = query("SELECT name FROM rit_team WHERE is_deleted = 0")
                if not team_members_df.empty:
                    for name in team_members_df['name']:
                        execute_silent(
                            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO notification_prefs (user_name, event_type, is_active) VALUES (?, 'RED_FLAG_ANOMALY', 1)",
                            (name,)
                        )
                logger.info("Seeded default notification preferences for RED_FLAG_ANOMALY.")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Error seeding default notification preferences for team: {e}")

        # Schedule job to run daily to create recurring tasks
        _scheduler.add_job(process_recurring_tasks, 'cron', hour=1, minute=0)  # type: ignore
        # Schedule job to run daily to check for upcoming tasks
        _scheduler.add_job(process_upcoming_task_alerts, 'cron', hour=8, minute=5)  # type: ignore
        # Schedule global vector store sync to run daily
        _scheduler.add_job(sync_all_data_to_global_vector_store, 'cron', hour=2, minute=0) # type: ignore
        # Schedule project health score calculation to run daily
        _scheduler.add_job(calculate_and_save_all_health_scores, 'cron', hour=4, minute=0) # Run daily at 4 AM
        # Schedule compliance checks to run daily
        _scheduler.add_job(run_compliance_checks, 'cron', hour=5, minute=0) # Run daily at 5 AM
        # Schedule the new AI agent to run daily
        _scheduler.add_job(run_ai_agent_assignments, 'cron', hour=6, minute=0) # Run daily at 6 AM
        # Schedule a daily email digest of unread notifications
        _scheduler.add_job(process_notification_digests, 'cron', hour=8, minute=30) # Run daily at 8:30 AM
        # Schedule KPI breach checks
        _scheduler.add_job(process_kpi_breach_alerts, 'cron', hour=9, minute=0) # Daily at 9 AM
        # Schedule nightly anomaly radar to run daily at 2:30 AM
        _scheduler.add_job(run_nightly_anomaly_radar, 'cron', hour=2, minute=30)
        
        # --- ADDED MAINTENANCE JOB ---
        # Schedule FTS index optimization to run weekly on Sunday at 1:00 AM
        _scheduler.add_job(optimize_fts_indexes, 'cron', day_of_week='sun', hour=1, minute=0) # type: ignore
        # Schedule weekly rolling database structure backup to run weekly on Sunday at 2:00 AM
        _scheduler.add_job(run_rolling_structure_backup, 'cron', day_of_week='sun', hour=2, minute=0) # type: ignore
        # Schedule weekly project status justification narrative generator to run weekly on Sunday at 3:00 AM
        _scheduler.add_job(run_weekly_status_justification_narratives, 'cron', day_of_week='sun', hour=3, minute=0) # type: ignore

        # Run nightly anomaly radar once on startup in a background thread
        import threading
        threading.Thread(target=run_nightly_anomaly_radar, name="AnomalyRadarOnStartup", daemon=True).start()
        # Run weekly status narratives once on startup in a background thread
        threading.Thread(target=run_weekly_status_justification_narratives, name="StatusNarrativesOnStartup", daemon=True).start()
        # Run weekly rolling database structure backup once on startup in a background thread
        threading.Thread(target=run_rolling_structure_backup, name="RollingStructureBackupOnStartup", daemon=True).start()

        _scheduler.start()  # type: ignore
        return _scheduler

def run_nightly_anomaly_radar():
    """
    Executes an evaluation scan against active database tables to identify stagnant tasks or communication blocks.
    Flags any active project stream that has not logged a meeting entry or an updated email log in 21 days
    while carrying unresolved overdue tasks.
    """
    logger.info("📡 Running nightly anomaly radar...")
    today = datetime.now()
    threshold_date = today - timedelta(days=21)
    
    try:
        # 1. Fetch all active projects
        projects_df = query(
            "SELECT id, name FROM projects WHERE is_deleted = 0 AND status NOT IN ('Complete', 'Withdrawn')"
        )
        if projects_df.empty:
            logger.info("No active projects found for anomaly check.")
            return

        import dateutil.parser as dparser

        for _, project in projects_df.iterrows():
            project_id = int(project['id'])
            project_name = project['name']

            # 2. Check meetings in the last 21 days
            meetings_df = query(
                "SELECT date FROM meetings WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", 
                (project_id,)
            )
            has_recent_meeting = False
            for _, row in meetings_df.iterrows():
                m_date = row['date']
                if m_date:
                    try:
                        parsed_date = dparser.parse(str(m_date))
                        if parsed_date.tzinfo is not None:
                            parsed_date = parsed_date.replace(tzinfo=None)
                        if parsed_date >= threshold_date:
                            has_recent_meeting = True
                            break
                    except Exception:
                        pass

            # 3. Check emails in the last 21 days
            emails_df = query(
                "SELECT date_sent FROM emails WHERE project_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", 
                (project_id,)
            )
            has_recent_email = False
            for _, row in emails_df.iterrows():
                e_date = row['date_sent']
                if e_date:
                    try:
                        parsed_date = dparser.parse(str(e_date))
                        if parsed_date.tzinfo is not None:
                            parsed_date = parsed_date.replace(tzinfo=None)
                        if parsed_date >= threshold_date:
                            has_recent_email = True
                            break
                    except Exception:
                        pass

            # 4. Check for unresolved tasks
            actions_df = query(
                "SELECT task FROM actions WHERE project_id = ? AND status != 'Closed' AND is_deleted = 0",
                (project_id,)
            )
            unresolved_tasks = actions_df['task'].tolist() if not actions_df.empty else []

            # 5. Check if stagnant and carrying unresolved tasks
            if not has_recent_meeting and not has_recent_email and len(unresolved_tasks) > 0:
                # Anomaly detected!
                logger.warning(f"🚨 Anomaly detected in project '{project_name}' (ID: {project_id})")
                
                task_summary = f"'{unresolved_tasks[0]}'"
                if len(unresolved_tasks) > 1:
                    task_summary += f" and {len(unresolved_tasks) - 1} other task(s)"
                
                message = (
                    f"RED FLAG ANOMALY: Project '{project_name}' is stagnant. "
                    f"No meetings or emails have been logged in the last 21 days, and the project "
                    f"carries {len(unresolved_tasks)} unresolved task(s) (including {task_summary}). "
                    f"Please check the project dashboard to address these communication and task blocks."
                )
                
                # Guard against duplicate notification in the last 24 hours
                last_notif = fetch_one(
                    "SELECT timestamp FROM notifications WHERE user_name = 'System' AND event_type = 'RED_FLAG_ANOMALY' AND project_id = ? ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1",
                    (project_id,)
                )
                if last_notif:
                    try:
                        last_notif_time = dparser.parse(str(last_notif[0]))
                        if last_notif_time.tzinfo is not None:
                            last_notif_time = last_notif_time.replace(tzinfo=None)
                        if (today - last_notif_time) < timedelta(days=1):
                            logger.info(f"Skipping duplicate anomaly alert for project '{project_name}' sent in the last 24h.")
                            continue
                    except Exception as e:
                        logger.error(f"Error parsing last notification time: {e}")

                # Insert critical notice to notifications table under System
                execute(
                    "INSERT INTO notifications (user_name, project_id, event_type, message, link, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (
                        "System",
                        project_id,
                        "RED_FLAG_ANOMALY",
                        message,
                        "pages/02_🔍_Project_Dashboard.py",
                        datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                    )
                )

                # Send notifications to project leads
                create_notifications_for_event(
                    event_type='RED_FLAG_ANOMALY',
                    message=message,
                    link="pages/02_🔍_Project_Dashboard.py",
                    project_id=project_id
                )
                logger.info(f"Successfully wrote critical notice to notifications table for project '{project_name}' and triggered notification delivery.")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Error executing nightly anomaly radar: {e}")
