# page_parts/project_dashboard/history.py
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import os
import dateutil.parser as dparser
from typing import Any, List, Dict
from datetime import datetime

# Modular Imports
from core.database_utils import query, execute, log_audit_event, execute_many, get_attachments_dir
from core.encryption_utils import decrypt_file
from core.auth_utils import user_can
from core.ai_utils import analyze_sentiment
from core.pdf_utils import export_minutes_to_word, generate_minutes_pdf

def _prepare_email_recipients_for_edit(field_value: Any, field_key: str, row_id: int, all_options: List[str], disabled_flag: bool) -> str:
    """Helper to render multiselect for email recipients in an edit form."""
    all_saved = [name.strip() for name in str(field_value).split(',')] if pd.notna(field_value) and field_value else []
    # Ensure options include any saved people, even if they've been removed from directories since
    options_with_current = sorted(list(set(all_options + all_saved)))

    selected = st.multiselect(f"{field_key.capitalize()}", options=options_with_current, default=all_saved, key=f"u_email_{field_key}_{row_id}", disabled=disabled_flag)
    other = st.text_input(f"Other '{field_key.capitalize()}' (comma-separated)", value=", ".join([name for name in all_saved if name not in options_with_current]), key=f"u_email_other_{field_key}_{row_id}", disabled=disabled_flag)

    final_list = selected
    if other:
        final_list.extend([name.strip() for name in other.split(',') if name.strip()])
    return ", ".join(sorted(list(set(final_list))))


def render(
    pid: int,
    current_user: str,
    current_user_role: str,
    all_attendees_options: List[str],
    prj_data: pd.Series,
    selected_prj: str,
    selected_org: str
):
    """Renders the project history feed tab."""
    st.subheader("📚 Project History Feed")

    # --- NEW: Search and Filter controls ---
    hist_c1, hist_c2 = st.columns([0.7, 0.3])
    history_search_query = hist_c1.text_input("Search history by keyword", key="history_search", label_visibility="collapsed", placeholder="Search history...")
    history_filter_type = hist_c2.radio(
        "Filter By:",
        ("All", "Meetings", "Emails"),
        horizontal=True,
        key="history_type_filter",
        label_visibility="collapsed"
    )

    # --- REVISED: Combine Meetings and Emails with Search ---
    df_meetings = pd.DataFrame()
    df_emails = pd.DataFrame()

    # Base SQL queries
    meeting_sql = """
        SELECT
            id, project_id, date, title, attendees, summary, thematic, decisions, next_steps, location, organizer, teams_url, start_time, end_time,
            consortium_notes, document_type, sentiment_score,
            'Meeting' as type,
            NULL as email_from, NULL as email_to, NULL as cc, NULL as body, NULL as influence_level
        FROM meetings WHERE project_id=? AND is_deleted=0
    """
    meeting_params: List[Any] = [pid]
    
    email_sql = """
        SELECT
            id, project_id, date_sent as date, subject as title,
            NULL as attendees, body as summary, NULL as thematic, NULL as decisions, NULL as next_steps, NULL as location, NULL as organizer, NULL as teams_url, NULL as start_time, NULL as end_time,
            NULL as consortium_notes, NULL as document_type, sentiment_score,
            'Email' as type,
            email_from, email_to, cc, body, influence_level
        FROM emails WHERE project_id=? AND is_deleted=0
    """
    email_params: List[Any] = [pid]

    if history_search_query:
        like_term = f"%{history_search_query}%"
        meeting_sql += " AND (title LIKE ? OR summary LIKE ? OR thematic LIKE ? OR decisions LIKE ? OR next_steps LIKE ?)"
        meeting_params.extend([like_term, like_term, like_term, like_term, like_term])
        
        email_sql += " AND (subject LIKE ? OR body LIKE ?)"
        email_params.extend([like_term, like_term])

    if history_filter_type in ("All", "Meetings"):
        df_meetings = query(meeting_sql, params=tuple(meeting_params))
    if history_filter_type in ("All", "Emails"):
        df_emails = query(email_sql, params=tuple(email_params))
    
    df_history = pd.concat([df_meetings, df_emails], ignore_index=True)
    if not df_history.empty:
        df_history['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df_history['date'], errors='coerce')
        df_history.sort_values(by='date', ascending=False, inplace=True)

    all_meeting_attachments_df = query("SELECT ma.* FROM meeting_attachments ma JOIN meetings m ON ma.meeting_id = m.id WHERE m.project_id = ? AND ma.is_deleted = 0", (pid,))
    meeting_attachments_map = all_meeting_attachments_df.groupby('meeting_id').apply(lambda x: x.to_dict('records')).to_dict()

    all_email_attachments_df = query("SELECT ea.* FROM email_attachments ea JOIN emails e ON ea.email_id = e.id WHERE e.project_id = ? AND ea.is_deleted = 0", (pid,))
    email_attachments_map = all_email_attachments_df.groupby('email_id').apply(lambda x: x.to_dict('records')).to_dict()

    all_other_projects_df = query("SELECT p.id, o.name as org_name, p.name as project_name FROM projects p JOIN orgs o ON p.org_id = o.id WHERE p.is_deleted = 0 AND o.is_deleted = 0 AND p.id != ? ORDER BY o.name, p.name", (pid,))

    if not df_history.empty:
        for _, row in df_history.iterrows():
            item_id = row['id']
            item_type = row['type']

            if item_type == 'Meeting':
                time_display = ""
                try:
                    if pd.notna(row.get('start_time')):
                        start_str = dparser.parse(row['start_time']).strftime('%H:%M')
                        end_str = ""
                        if pd.notna(row.get('end_time')):
                            end_str = dparser.parse(row['end_time']).strftime(' - %H:%M')
                        time_display = f" | 🕒 {start_str}{end_str}"
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    pass

                date_str = row['date'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d') if pd.notna(row['date']) else 'No Date'
                exp_title = f"📅 {date_str}{time_display} | {row.get('title') or '(No Title)'}"
                with st.expander(exp_title):
                    st.write("**Attachments**")
                    attachments = meeting_attachments_map.get(item_id, [])
                    if attachments:
                        for i, att_row in enumerate(attachments):
                            if att_row['file_path'] and pd.notna(att_row['file_path']) and os.path.exists(att_row['file_path']):
                                try:
                                    decrypted_bytes = decrypt_file(att_row['file_path'])
                                    st.download_button(f"📎 {att_row['file_name']}", decrypted_bytes, file_name=att_row['file_name'], key=f"dl_att_{att_row['id']}_{i}")
                                except Exception:
                                    st.caption(f"📎 {att_row['file_name']} (Decrypt Fail)")

                    dl_single_c1, dl_single_c2 = st.columns(2)
                    with dl_single_c1:
                        single_word_bytes = export_minutes_to_word(pd.DataFrame([row]), selected_prj, selected_org)
                        st.download_button("📄 Export to Word", data=single_word_bytes, file_name=f"Minute_{selected_org}_{selected_prj}_{row['date']}.docx", mime="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document", key=f"dl_single_minute_word_{row['id']}", use_container_width=True)
                    with dl_single_c2:
                        single_pdf_bytes = generate_minutes_pdf(pd.DataFrame([row]), selected_prj, selected_org)
                        st.download_button("📄 Export to PDF", data=single_pdf_bytes, file_name=f"Minute_{selected_org}_{selected_prj}_{row['date']}.pdf", mime="application/pdf", key=f"dl_single_minute_pdf_{row['id']}", use_container_width=True)
                    st.divider()

                    st.markdown(f"##### Meeting Title: {row.get('title') or '(No Title)'}")
                    if row.get('location'): st.caption(f"📍 **Location:** {row.get('location')}")
                    if row.get('organizer'): st.caption(f"👤 **Organizer:** {row.get('organizer')}")
                    if pd.notna(row.get('teams_url')) and row['teams_url']: st.caption(f"🔗 [Microsoft Teams Link]({row['teams_url']})")
                    if any([row.get('location'), row.get('organizer'), row.get('teams_url')]): st.divider()

                    st.markdown("##### Executive Summary")
                    st.markdown(row['summary'] or "_No summary provided._")
                    st.markdown("##### Thematic Discussion")
                    st.markdown(row['thematic'] or "_No thematic discussion provided._")
                    st.markdown("##### Decisions Made")
                    st.markdown(row['decisions'] or "_No decisions provided._")
                    st.markdown("##### Strategic Outlook")
                    st.markdown(row['next_steps'] or "_No outlook provided._")

                    if prj_data['name'] == "Foundational Readiness" and pd.notna(row.get('consortium_notes')) and row.get('consortium_notes'):
                        st.markdown("##### Consortium Notes")
                        st.markdown(row['consortium_notes'])

                    st.divider()
                    if st.button("Manage Minute", key=f"manage_minute_{item_id}", use_container_width=True):
                        st.session_state['modal_edit_entity'] = {
                            "type": "meeting", "data": row.to_dict(),
                            "additional_data": {"all_attendees_options": all_attendees_options, "all_other_projects_df": all_other_projects_df, "project_name": prj_data['name']}
                        }
                        st.rerun()

            elif item_type == 'Email':
                sentiment = row['sentiment_score'] if pd.notna(row['sentiment_score']) else 0.0
                icon = "🚨" if sentiment < -0.1 else "✉️"
                date_str = row['date'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d') if pd.notna(row.get('date')) else 'No Date'
                exp_title = f"{icon} Email: {date_str} | {row.get('title') or '(No Subject)'}"
                with st.expander(exp_title):
                    cc_display = f" | CC: {row['cc']}" if pd.notna(row.get('cc')) and row['cc'] else ""
                    
                    with st.container(border=True):
                        st.caption(f"From: {row.get('email_from') or 'N/A'} | To: {row.get('email_to') or 'N/A'}{cc_display} | On: {date_str}")
                        st.markdown(row['body'])

                    thread_df = query("SELECT * FROM email_thread WHERE email_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0 ORDER BY date ASC", (item_id,))
                    for _, reply in thread_df.iterrows():
                        with st.container(border=True):
                            author_label = "My Reply" if reply['author'] == "Me" else f"Reply from {reply['author']}"
                            st.caption(f"**{author_label}** on {reply['date']}")
                            st.caption(f"To: {reply.get('to_recipients') or 'N/A'} | CC: {reply.get('cc_recipients') or 'N/A'}")
                            st.markdown(reply['body'])
                    
                    attachments = email_attachments_map.get(item_id, [])
                    if attachments:
                        st.write("**Attachments**")
                        for att_row in attachments:
                            if att_row['file_path'] and pd.notna(att_row['file_path']) and os.path.exists(att_row['file_path']):
                                try:
                                    decrypted_bytes = decrypt_file(att_row['file_path'])
                                    st.download_button(f"📎 {att_row['file_name']}", decrypted_bytes, file_name=att_row['file_name'], key=f"dl_hist_email_att_{att_row['id']}")
                                except Exception as e:
                                    st.error(f"Could not decrypt file: {e}")
                    st.divider()

                    with st.expander("✏️ Edit this Email Log"):
                        with st.form(key=f"edit_email_{row['id']}"):
                            can_edit_email, reason = user_can("edit_meeting")

                            edit_d1, edit_d2 = st.columns(2)
                            curr_date_sent = pd.to_datetime(row['date']).date() if pd.notna(row['date']) else None
                            u_date_sent = edit_d1.date_input("Date Sent", value=curr_date_sent, key=f"u_email_date_{row['id']}", disabled=not can_edit_email)
                            u_subject = edit_d2.text_input("Subject", value=row['title'], key=f"u_email_subj_{row['id']}", disabled=not can_edit_email)

                            with st.expander("Sender & Recipients"):
                                u_from = _prepare_email_recipients_for_edit(row['email_from'], 'from', row['id'], all_attendees_options, not can_edit_email)
                                u_to = _prepare_email_recipients_for_edit(row['email_to'], 'to', row['id'], all_attendees_options, not can_edit_email)
                                u_cc = _prepare_email_recipients_for_edit(row['cc'], 'cc', row['id'], all_attendees_options, not can_edit_email)
                            u_body = st.text_area("Email Body", value=row['body'], height=200, key=f"u_email_body_{row['id']}", disabled=not can_edit_email)

                            st.divider()
                            st.markdown("##### 🎯 Strategic Analysis")
                            u_influence = st.select_slider("Sender Influence", options=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5], value=int(row.get('influence_level') or 3), key=f"u_email_influence_{row['id']}", disabled=not can_edit_email)
                            
                            if st.form_submit_button("💾 Save Email Changes", type="primary", disabled=not can_edit_email):
                                new_sentiment = analyze_sentiment(u_body)['polarity'] if u_body != row['body'] else row['sentiment_score']
                                date_to_save = str(u_date_sent) if u_date_sent else None
                                execute("UPDATE emails SET date_sent=?, subject=?, email_from=?, email_to=?, cc=?, body=?, influence_level=?, sentiment_score=? WHERE id=?",
                                        (date_to_save, u_subject, u_from, u_to, u_cc, u_body, u_influence, new_sentiment, row['id']))
                                log_audit_event("UPDATE", "Email", current_user, current_user_role, row['id'], details={"subject": u_subject})
                                st.toast("Email log updated successfully!")
                                st.rerun()
                
                    with st.form(f"add_reply_{item_id}", clear_on_submit=True):
                        st.markdown("##### 💬 Add to Thread")
                        reply_author_input = st.selectbox("Author of this reply", ["Me", "Other..."], key=f"reply_author_{item_id}")
                        reply_author_name = "Me"
                        if reply_author_input == "Other...":
                            reply_author_name = st.text_input("Sender Name", key=f"reply_sender_name_{item_id}")

                        reply_to_list = st.multiselect("To", options=all_attendees_options, key=f"reply_to_list_{item_id}")
                        reply_cc_list = st.multiselect("CC", options=all_attendees_options, key=f"reply_cc_list_{item_id}")
                        reply_date = st.date_input("Date of Reply", value=datetime.now().date(), key=f"reply_date_{item_id}")
                        reply_body = st.text_area("Reply Body", key=f"reply_body_{item_id}")

                        if st.form_submit_button("Add Reply"):
                            if reply_body and reply_author_name:
                                reply_sentiment = analyze_sentiment(reply_body)['polarity']
                                execute("INSERT INTO email_thread (email_id, author, date, body, to_recipients, cc_recipients, sentiment_score) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                                        (item_id, reply_author_name, str(reply_date), reply_body, ",".join(reply_to_list), ",".join(reply_cc_list), reply_sentiment))
                                st.rerun()

                    if user_can("delete_meeting"):
                        if st.button("🗑️ Delete Full Log Entry", key=f"del_hist_email_{row['id']}"):
                            execute("UPDATE emails SET is_deleted=1 WHERE id=?", (row['id'],))
                            st.rerun()
    else:
        st.info("No history recorded for this stream.")

import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from core.ai_utils import answer_document_question

class TestDocumentQA(unittest.TestCase):
    @patch('core.ai_utils.generate_ai_response')
    def test_answer_document_question(self, mock_generate):
        # Set up mock response
        mock_generate.return_value = "Mocked LLM Answer"
        
        # Inputs
        query = "What is the policy name?"
        context = "This policy is named NHS Reference Guide 2026."
        
        # Call function
        result = answer_document_question(query, context)
        
        # Verify
        mock_generate.assert_called_once()
        self.assertEqual(result, "Mocked LLM Answer")
        
        # Inspect system prompt argument
        called_args, called_kwargs = mock_generate.call_args
        # The prompt is passed as a keyword argument
        self.assertEqual(called_kwargs.get('prompt'), query)
        
        # The system prompt should contain the context
        system_prompt = called_kwargs.get('system_prompt')
        self.assertIn("NHS Reference Guide 2026", system_prompt)
        self.assertEqual(called_kwargs.get('temperature'), 0.1)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

    @classmethod

    def test_weekly_status_narratives_generation(self):
        # 1. Create a mock organization and active project
        org_id = execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO orgs (name, region) VALUES (?, ?)", ("Test Weekly Org", "North East"), return_lastrowid=True)
        if not org_id:
            # fetch the existing one
            org_row = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM orgs WHERE name = ?", ("Test Weekly Org",))
            org_id = org_row[0]

        project_id = execute(
            "INSERT INTO projects (org_id, name, status, rag_status, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (org_id, "Test Weekly status Project", "Active", "Amber",),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )

        # 2. Seed project_milestones
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, actual_date, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (project_id, "Milestone 1", "2026-06-01", "2026-06-02", "Achieved")
        )
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, actual_date, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (project_id, "Milestone 2", "2026-06-15", None, "Delayed")
        )

        # 3. Seed risks
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO risks (project_id, description, impact, mitigation, status, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "High clinical safety risk", "High", "Regular audits", "Open")
        )

        # 4. Seed actions (tasks completed and open)
        # Completed in last 4 weeks
        today_str = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO actions (project_id, task, status, due_date, date_completed, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "Task 1", "Closed", today_str, today_str)
        )
        # Open tasks
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO actions (project_id, task, status, due_date, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "Task 2", "Open", today_str)
        )

        # 5. Seed emails and meetings to calculate sentiment shifts
        # Recent email
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO emails (project_id, subject, body, date_sent, sentiment_score, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "Status Update", "Great progress is being made on the rollout.", today_str, 0.8)
        )
        # Historical meeting
        old_date = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=20)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO meetings (project_id, date, summary, sentiment_score, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, old_date, "Project starting up. Some concerns raised.", -0.2)
        )

        # 6. Run the generation loop!
        from unittest.mock import patch

            execute("DELETE FROM ai_project_status_drafts WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
            
            # Execute narrative generation
            generate_weekly_project_status_narratives()

            drafts_df = query("SELECT draft_narrative, created_at, rag_status FROM ai_project_status_drafts WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
            self.assertFalse(drafts_df.empty, "Draft was not inserted into database")

            self.assertEqual(drafts_df.iloc[0]['rag_status'], "Amber")
            
            # Verify prompt contains our parameters
            called_args, called_kwargs = mock_gen.call_args
            prompt_sent = called_kwargs.get('prompt') or called_args[0]
            self.assertIn("Milestone 2", prompt_sent)
            self.assertIn("High clinical safety risk", prompt_sent)
            self.assertIn("Weekly velocity: 0.25 tasks/week", prompt_sent)
            self.assertIn("Sentiment Shift: +1.00", prompt_sent) # 0.8 recent - (-0.2 historical) = +1.00

        # Clean up mock project data
        execute("DELETE FROM project_milestones WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM risks WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM actions WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM emails WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM meetings WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM ai_project_status_drafts WHERE project_id = ?", (project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?", (project_id,))

### FILE: tests/test_database_encryption.py
==================================================

import unittest
import os
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from core.database_utils import (
    execute,
    fetch_one,
    get_connection,
    save_db_to_disk,
    ensure_db_initialized,
    DB_PATH
)
from core.encryption_utils import get_encryption_key, decrypt_data, encrypt_data

class TestDatabaseEncryption(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # We want to use a separate test db file so we don't mess up projects.db during test
        self.original_db_path = DB_PATH
        self.test_db_file = Path(self.original_db_path).parent / "test_projects_encrypt.db"
        if self.test_db_file.exists():
            self.test_db_file.unlink()
        self.reset_db_state()

    def reset_db_state(self):
        import core.database_utils
        # Dispose the SQLAlchemy engine to close all pooled connections
        try:
            engine = core.database_utils.get_engine()
            engine.dispose()
        except Exception:
            pass
        try:
            core.database_utils.get_engine.cache_clear()
        except Exception:
            pass
        
        # Close and reset the global in-memory connection
        if core.database_utils._mem_db_connection:
            try:
                core.database_utils._mem_db_connection.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
        core.database_utils._mem_db_connection = None
        core.database_utils._initialized = False

    def tearDown(self):
        # Clean up test file
        if self.test_db_file.exists():
            self.test_db_file.unlink()
        temp_file = self.test_db_file.with_suffix(".tmp")
        if temp_file.exists():
            temp_file.unlink()

        # Restore original state
        import core.database_utils
        core.database_utils.DB_PATH = self.original_db_path
        self.reset_db_state()
        try:
            core.database_utils.ensure_db_initialized()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def test_database_encryption_flow(self):
        # Let's temporarily override core.database_utils.DB_PATH to point to our test database file
        import core.database_utils
        core.database_utils.DB_PATH = str(self.test_db_file)
        
        self.reset_db_state()
        
        # 1. Initialize empty DB on the new test path
        ensure_db_initialized()
        
        # Create a table and insert a row in-memory
        with get_connection() as conn:
            conn.execute("CREATE TABLE encrypt_test (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)")
            conn.execute("INSERT INTO encrypt_test (name) VALUES ('Secret Stakeholder')")
            conn.commit()
            
        # Manually force save to disk for synchronous verification in test
        save_db_to_disk()
        
        # Verify the file exists on disk
        self.assertTrue(self.test_db_file.exists())
        
        # Verify that the file on disk is NOT a plaintext SQLite database
        with open(self.test_db_file, "rb") as f:
            file_data = f.read()
        self.assertFalse(file_data.startswith(b"SQLite format 3\x00"))
        
        # Try to decrypt the file data manually to verify it contains valid SQLite data
        decrypted = decrypt_data(file_data)
        self.assertTrue(decrypted.startswith(b"SQLite format 3\x00"))
        
        # 2. Reset connection and state, and reload to test transparent decryption
        self.reset_db_state()
        
        ensure_db_initialized()
        with get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute("SELECT name FROM encrypt_test")
            row = cursor.fetchone()
            self.assertIsNotNone(row)
            self.assertEqual(row[0], "Secret Stakeholder")
            
        # 3. Test legacy unencrypted database migration
        self.reset_db_state()
        if self.test_db_file.exists():
            self.test_db_file.unlink()
        
        raw_conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.test_db_file))
        raw_conn.execute("CREATE TABLE legacy_test (val TEXT)")
        raw_conn.execute("INSERT INTO legacy_test VALUES ('Unencrypted Data')")
        raw_conn.commit()
        raw_conn.close()
        
        # Check that it starts with the SQLite magic header
        with open(self.test_db_file, "rb") as f:
            raw_data = f.read()
        self.assertTrue(raw_data.startswith(b"SQLite format 3\x00"))
        
        # Now trigger initialization. It should automatically detect, encrypt, and load it!
        ensure_db_initialized()
        
        # Check that the file on disk is now encrypted (does not start with SQLite format 3)
        with open(self.test_db_file, "rb") as f:
            migrated_data = f.read()
        self.assertFalse(migrated_data.startswith(b"SQLite format 3\x00"))
        
        # Verify the data was loaded correctly into memory
        with get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute("SELECT val FROM legacy_test")
            row = cursor.fetchone()
            self.assertIsNotNone(row)
            self.assertEqual(row[0], "Unencrypted Data")

    def test_wal_journal_mode_enforcement(self):
        import core.database_utils
        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event
        
        # Test 1: Check that connections from get_connection() have synchronous=1 (NORMAL)
        with get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute("PRAGMA synchronous;")
            sync_val = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            # 1 corresponds to NORMAL (0=OFF, 1=NORMAL, 2=FULL, 3=EXTRA)
            self.assertEqual(sync_val, 1)
            
            cursor.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode;")
            journal_val = cursor.fetchone()[0]
            # Since the global connection is in-memory, SQLite will report 'memory'
            # (as it overrides 'wal' for in-memory databases)
            self.assertIn(journal_val, ("memory", "wal"))
            
        # Test 2: Verify that for a file-based SQLite database, 'wal' mode is actually set successfully
        test_file_db = Path(core.database_utils.DB_PATH).parent / "test_wal_mode.db"
        if test_file_db.exists():
            test_file_db.unlink()
            
        try:
            # Create a file-based engine
            file_engine = create_engine(
                f"sqlite:///{test_file_db}",
                connect_args={'check_same_thread': False}
            )
            
            # Register our event listener on this file engine
            @event.listens_for(file_engine, "connect")
            def set_sqlite_pragma(dbapi_connection, connection_record):
                cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
                cursor.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
                cursor.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;")
                cursor.close()
                
            # Verify that connection from this engine has journal_mode=wal
            with file_engine.connect() as conn:
                res = conn.exec_driver_sql("PRAGMA journal_mode;").fetchone()
                self.assertEqual(res[0], "wal")
                sync_res = conn.exec_driver_sql("PRAGMA synchronous;").fetchone()
                self.assertEqual(sync_res[0], 1)
        finally:
            if test_file_db.exists():
                try:
                    test_file_db.unlink()
                except Exception:
                    pass

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# tests/test_archive_utils.py
import unittest

import pandas as pd
from unittest.mock import patch

from core.database_utils import execute, query, run_migrations
from core.archive_utils import build_user_archive

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class TestArchiveUtils(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        import shutil
        import os
        import core.database_utils
        # Redirect to a temporary test database file to isolate test executions
        cls.original_db_path = core.database_utils.DB_PATH
        cls.test_db_path = core.database_utils.DB_PATH.replace("projects.db", "projects_test.db")
        
        # Copy the active database schema & content as the starting point for test database
        if os.path.exists(cls.original_db_path):
            shutil.copy(cls.original_db_path, cls.test_db_path)
            # Remove any copied journal files to avoid SQLite locks/mismatches
            for ext in ["-wal", "-shm"]:
                wal_path = cls.test_db_path + ext
                if os.path.exists(wal_path):
                    try:
                        os.remove(wal_path)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                        
        core.database_utils.DB_PATH = cls.test_db_path
        core.database_utils.get_engine.cache_clear()
        
        # Run migrations to ensure database tables are created
        run_migrations()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        import os
        import core.database_utils
        # Restore the original active database path
        core.database_utils.DB_PATH = cls.original_db_path
        core.database_utils.get_engine.cache_clear()
        
        # Clean up the temporary test database files
        for ext in ["", "-wal", "-shm"]:
            path = cls.test_db_path + ext
            if os.path.exists(path):
                try:
                    os.remove(path)
                except Exception:
                    pass

    def test_build_user_archive_empty(self):
        # Test archive generation when there is no data for the user
        zip_bytes, filename = build_user_archive("Nonexistent User", user_id=999)
        self.assertIsInstance(zip_bytes, bytes)
        self.assertTrue(filename.startswith("personal_archive_"))
        self.assertTrue(filename.endswith(".zip"))

        # Verify the ZIP contents
        zip_buffer = io.BytesIO(zip_bytes)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_buffer, 'r') as zf:
            namelist = zf.namelist()
            expected_files = [
                "meetings/meetings.csv",
                "meetings/meetings.json",
                "tasks/tasks.csv",
                "tasks/tasks.json",
                "risks/risks.csv",
                "risks/risks.json",
                "emails/emails.csv",
                "emails/emails.json",
                "stakeholders/stakeholders.csv",
                "stakeholders/stakeholders.json",
                "MANIFEST.txt"
            ]
            for ef in expected_files:
                self.assertIn(ef, namelist)

            # Check that files are empty (CSV has only headers, JSON has empty array '[]')
            meetings_csv = zf.read("meetings/meetings.csv").decode("utf-8").strip()
            # For a DataFrame with columns and no rows, pandas to_csv outputs the header
            self.assertTrue(len(meetings_csv) > 0) # contains headers

            meetings_json = zf.read("meetings/meetings.json").decode("utf-8").strip()
            self.assertEqual(meetings_json, "[]")

            manifest = zf.read("MANIFEST.txt").decode("utf-8")
            self.assertTrue(any(line.strip().startswith("Meetings") and "0 record(s)" in line for line in manifest.splitlines()))
            self.assertTrue(any(line.strip().startswith("Tasks") and "0 record(s)" in line for line in manifest.splitlines()))
            self.assertTrue(any(line.strip().startswith("Risks") and "0 record(s)" in line for line in manifest.splitlines()))
            self.assertTrue(any(line.strip().startswith("Emails") and "0 record(s)" in line for line in manifest.splitlines()))
            self.assertTrue(any(line.strip().startswith("Stakeholders") and "0 record(s)" in line for line in manifest.splitlines()))

    def test_build_user_archive_success(self):
        # 1. Seed some mock data
        org_id = execute("INSERT INTO orgs (name, region) VALUES (?, ?)", ("Test Org", "North East"), return_lastrowid=True)
        project_id = execute("INSERT INTO projects (org_id, name, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (org_id, "Test Project", "Active"), return_lastrowid=True)

        user_name = "Archive Test User"
        user_id = execute("INSERT INTO rit_team (name, primary_role) VALUES (?, ?)", (user_name, "Advisor"), return_lastrowid=True)

        # Connect user to project in resource_allocations (assuming this table connects them)
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO resource_allocations (user_id, project_id, allocation_pct, start_date) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (user_id, project_id, 100, "2026-07-06")
        )

        # Seed meeting (user organizer)
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO meetings (project_id, date, title, organizer, attendees, summary, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "2026-07-01", "Mock Meeting", user_name, "Attendee A", "Some notes")
        )

        # Seed task (assigned to user)
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO actions (project_id, task, assigned_to, due_date, status, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "Mock Task", user_name, "2026-07-10", "Open")
        )

        # Seed risk (owned by user)
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO risks (project_id, category, description, risk_score, owner, status, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, "Resource", "Mock Risk", 12, user_name, "Open")
        )

        # Seed email (from user)
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO emails (project_id, email_from, email_to, subject, body, date_sent, is_deleted) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
            (project_id, f"{user_name} <user@test.com>", "receiver@test.com", "Mock Email", "Mock email body", "2026-07-06 12:00:00")
        )

        # Seed contact and stakeholder
        contact_id = execute(

        )
        execute(

            (project_id, contact_id, "High", "Medium", "Neutral", 80.0)
        )

        # 2. Run builder
        zip_bytes, filename = build_user_archive(user_name, user_id=user_id)
        self.assertIsInstance(zip_bytes, bytes)
        self.assertTrue(len(zip_bytes) > 0)

        # 3. Verify ZIP contents and that they contain the seeded data

            risks_json = zf.read("risks/risks.json").decode("utf-8")
            self.assertIn("Mock Risk", risks_json)

            emails_json = zf.read("emails/emails.json").decode("utf-8")
            self.assertIn("Mock Email", emails_json)

            # Let's check stakeholders. If project_team_members fails, stakeholders might be empty.
            # We want to check if they are fetched correctly or if there is a warning.
            stakeholders_json = zf.read("stakeholders/stakeholders.json").decode("utf-8")
            logger.info("Stakeholders json output: %s", stakeholders_json)

        self.assertIn("checkSession()", js_code)

    def test_run_adkar_stance_risk_modeler(self):
        """Verifies ADKAR stance risk modeler returns correct risk levels, scores, and mitigation signals."""
        # 1. Insert a contact
        contact_id = execute(
            "INSERT INTO contacts (name, job_title, email, org_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            ("John Blocker", "IT Director", "john.blocker@nhs.net", self.org_id),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        # 2. Insert a stakeholder with High influence, Medium interest, Blocker stance
        # ADKAR scores: Awareness=4, Desire=2, Knowledge=5, Ability=4, Reinforcement=5
        # Mapped scores: Influence (3) * Interest (2) * Stance (5) = 30 -> High Risk
        # First barrier under 3: Desire (2)
        sh_id = execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO stakeholders (
                project_id, contact_id, influence, interest, current_stance,
                adkar_awareness, adkar_desire, adkar_knowledge, adkar_ability, adkar_reinforcement
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (self.project_id, contact_id, "High", "Medium", "Blocker", 4, 2, 5, 4, 5),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        try:
            # Run modeler
            signals = run_adkar_stance_risk_modeler(self.project_id)
            
            # Check results
            self.assertEqual(len(signals), 1)
            sig = signals[0]
            self.assertEqual(sig['stakeholder_name'], "John Blocker")
            self.assertEqual(sig['job_title'], "IT Director")
            self.assertEqual(sig['influence_score'], 3)
            self.assertEqual(sig['interest_score'], 2)
            self.assertEqual(sig['stance_score'], 5)
            self.assertEqual(sig['stance_risk_score'], 30)
            self.assertEqual(sig['risk_level'], "High")
            self.assertEqual(sig['barrier_point'], "Desire")
            self.assertEqual(sig['barrier_score'], 2)
            self.assertIn("Desire Gap: Low motivation to participate.", sig['mitigation_signal'])
            self.assertEqual(sig['escalation_required'], 1)
        finally:
            # Clean up
            execute("DELETE FROM stakeholders WHERE id = ?", (sh_id,))
            execute("DELETE FROM contacts WHERE id = ?", (contact_id,))

    def test_affected_trusts(self):
        """Verifies emails and email_thread affected_trusts field is correctly saved and retrieved."""
        import json
        test_trusts = ["Trust A", "Trust B"]
        trusts_json = json.dumps(test_trusts)
        
        email_id = execute(
            """INSERT INTO emails (project_id, email_from, email_to, cc, subject, body, date_sent, sentiment_score, influence_level, thread_group_id, affected_trusts)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (self.project_id, "from@example.com", "to@example.com", "", "Test Trusts Subject", "Body text", "2026-07-03 12:00:00", 0.0, 3, "group-123", trusts_json),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        reply_id = execute(
            """INSERT INTO email_thread (email_id, author, date, body, to_recipients, cc_recipients, sentiment_score, affected_trusts)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (email_id, "Author A", "2026-07-03 12:05:00", "Reply body", "to@example.com", "", 0.0, trusts_json),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        try:
            # Query emails
            email_row = query("SELECT affected_trusts FROM emails WHERE id = ?", (email_id,))
            self.assertFalse(email_row.empty)
            saved_trusts_email = json.loads(email_row.iloc[0, 0])
            self.assertEqual(saved_trusts_email, test_trusts)
            
            # Query email_thread
            reply_row = query("SELECT affected_trusts FROM email_thread WHERE id = ?", (reply_id,))
            self.assertFalse(reply_row.empty)
            saved_trusts_reply = json.loads(reply_row.iloc[0, 0])
            self.assertEqual(saved_trusts_reply, test_trusts)
        finally:
            execute("DELETE FROM email_thread WHERE id = ?", (reply_id,))
            execute("DELETE FROM emails WHERE id = ?", (email_id,))

    def test_run_executive_sentiment_shift_tracker(self):
        """Verifies that run_executive_sentiment_shift_tracker correctly identifies a sharp drop in stakeholder sentiment."""
        from datetime import timedelta
        
        # 1. Insert a contact with an executive role title
        contact_id = execute(
            "INSERT INTO contacts (name, job_title, email, org_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
            ("Jane Exec", "Chief Executive", "jane.exec@nhs.net", self.org_id),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        # 2. Insert a stakeholder linked to this contact
        sh_id = execute(
            "INSERT INTO stakeholders (project_id, contact_id, influence, interest, current_stance) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (self.project_id, contact_id, "High", "High", "Supporter"),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        # We will seed two emails:
        # Email A: 25 days ago (historical, week 4) with positive sentiment (+0.8)
        # Email B: 3 days ago (recent, week 1) with negative sentiment (-0.6)
        # Delta = -0.6 - 0.8 = -1.4 (sharp drop)
        ref_now = datetime.now()
        date_wk4 = (ref_now - timedelta(days=25)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        date_wk1 = (ref_now - timedelta(days=3)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        
        email_wk4_id = execute(
            """INSERT INTO emails (project_id, email_from, email_to, subject, body, date_sent, sentiment_score, is_deleted)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)""",
            (self.project_id, "jane.exec@nhs.net", "to@example.com", "Great Progress", "Everything is on track.", date_wk4, 0.8),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        email_wk1_id = execute(
            """INSERT INTO emails (project_id, email_from, email_to, subject, body, date_sent, sentiment_score, is_deleted)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0)""",
            (self.project_id, "jane.exec@nhs.net", "to@example.com", "System Down", "This is very disappointing.", date_wk1, -0.6),
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        
        try:
            # Run tracker
            flagged = run_executive_sentiment_shift_tracker(project_id=self.project_id, threshold=-0.3)
            
            # Assertions
            self.assertEqual(len(flagged), 1)
            f = flagged[0]
            self.assertEqual(f['name'], "Jane Exec")
            self.assertEqual(f['job_title'], "Chief Executive")
            self.assertTrue(f['is_executive'])
            self.assertEqual(f['recent_avg'], -0.6)
            self.assertEqual(f['historical_avg'], 0.8)
            self.assertEqual(f['sentiment_drop'], -1.4)
        finally:
            # Clean up
            execute("DELETE FROM emails WHERE id IN (?, ?)", (email_wk4_id, email_wk1_id))
            execute("DELETE FROM stakeholders WHERE id = ?", (sh_id,))
            execute("DELETE FROM contacts WHERE id = ?", (contact_id,))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import sys
import unittest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

# Save original modules before mocking
_original_modules = {}
for m in ['streamlit', 'chromadb', 'ollama', 'core.database_utils']:
    if m in sys.modules:
        _original_modules[m] = sys.modules[m]

# Mock dependencies before importing core.ai_utils
mock_streamlit = MagicMock()
mock_streamlit.session_state = {}
sys.modules['streamlit'] = mock_streamlit

mock_chromadb = MagicMock()
sys.modules['chromadb'] = mock_chromadb

mock_ollama = MagicMock()
sys.modules['ollama'] = mock_ollama

mock_database_utils = MagicMock()
sys.modules['core.database_utils'] = mock_database_utils

# Import the functions under test
from core.ai_utils import (
    anonymize_payload,
    unmask_stream,
    get_db_pii_names,
    generate_ai_response,
    stream_ai_response,
    is_privacy_masking_enabled
)

class TestPrivacyMasking(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_anonymize_payload_basic(self):
        text = "Hello John Smith. My email is john.smith@example.com and number is +447712345678."
        db_names = ["John Smith"]
        
        orig_to_mask = {}
        mask_to_original = {}
        
        anonymized = anonymize_payload(text, orig_to_mask, mask_to_original, db_names)
        
        # Verify placeholders are substituted
        self.assertIn("[STAFF_1]", anonymized)
        self.assertIn("[EMAIL_1]", anonymized)
        self.assertIn("[PHONE_1]", anonymized)
        self.assertNotIn("John Smith", anonymized)
        self.assertNotIn("john.smith@example.com", anonymized)
        self.assertNotIn("+447712345678", anonymized)
        
        # Verify mapping contents
        self.assertEqual(orig_to_mask["John Smith"], "[STAFF_1]")
        self.assertEqual(orig_to_mask["john.smith@example.com"], "[EMAIL_1]")
        self.assertEqual(orig_to_mask["+447712345678"], "[PHONE_1]")
        
        self.assertEqual(mask_to_original["[STAFF_1]"], "John Smith")
        self.assertEqual(mask_to_original["[EMAIL_1]"], "john.smith@example.com")
        self.assertEqual(mask_to_original["[PHONE_1]"], "+447712345678")

    def test_anonymize_payload_case_sensitive_components(self):
        # "Sarah Jenkins" matches full name case-insensitively, but "Sarah" alone matches case-sensitively
        text = "Sarah told Sarah Jenkins that she will meet Will later today."
        db_names = ["Sarah Jenkins", "Will Power"] # "Will" is in common blocklist so "Will" as component shouldn't match case-insensitively, and shouldn't match if lowercase
        
        orig_to_mask = {}
        mask_to_original = {}
        
        anonymized = anonymize_payload(text, orig_to_mask, mask_to_original, db_names)
        
        # "Sarah Jenkins" should be STAFF_1
        # "Sarah" should also be STAFF_1 (since she is Sarah Jenkins)
        self.assertIn("[STAFF_1]", anonymized)
        self.assertNotIn("Sarah Jenkins", anonymized)
        self.assertNotIn("Sarah told", anonymized)
        
        # "will" should NOT be masked because it is lowercase and is a common word
        self.assertIn("she will meet", anonymized)
        
        # "Will" (capitalized) should be STAFF_2 (since we have Will Power in DB)
        self.assertIn("meet [STAFF_2] later", anonymized)

    def test_unmask_stream(self):
        stream_chunks = ["Hello ", "[ST", "AFF_1], ", "my email ", "is [EMAIL_1] and ", "phone is [PHONE_1]."]
        mapping = {
            "[STAFF_1]": "John Smith",
            "[EMAIL_1]": "john.smith@example.com",
            "[PHONE_1]": "+447712345678"
        }
        
        unmasked = list(unmask_stream(stream_chunks, mapping))
        result = "".join(unmasked)
        
        self.assertEqual(result, "Hello John Smith, my email is john.smith@example.com and phone is +447712345678.")

    @patch('core.ai_utils.query')
    def test_get_db_pii_names(self, mock_query):
        import pandas as pd
        # Mock various tables queries
        def side_effect(sql, *args, **kwargs):
            if "rit_team" in sql:
                return pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Alice Smith", "Bob Jones"]})
            elif "contacts" in sql:
                return pd.DataFrame({"name": ["Dr. Charles Xavier", "Emma Frost"]})
            elif "actions" in sql:
                return pd.DataFrame({"assigned_to": ["Alice Smith, Emma Frost", "Unknown"]})
            elif "risks" in sql:
                return pd.DataFrame({"owner": ["Bob Jones", "Admin"]})
            return pd.DataFrame()
            
        mock_query.side_effect = side_effect
        names = get_db_pii_names()
        
        # Verify names are collected and filtered
        self.assertIn("Alice Smith", names)
        self.assertIn("Bob Jones", names)
        self.assertIn("Dr. Charles Xavier", names)
        self.assertIn("Emma Frost", names)
        self.assertNotIn("Unknown", names)
        self.assertNotIn("Admin", names)

    @patch('core.ai_utils.is_privacy_masking_enabled')
    @patch('core.ai_utils.get_db_pii_names')
    @patch('ollama.chat')
    def test_generate_ai_response_with_masking(self, mock_chat, mock_get_names, mock_enabled):
        mock_enabled.return_value = True
        mock_get_names.return_value = ["Alice Smith"]
        
        # Mock Ollama chat response containing the mask
        mock_chat.return_value = {
            "message": {
                "content": "Sure, I can help [STAFF_1] with their request."
            }
        }
        
        response = generate_ai_response(
            prompt="Hello Alice Smith",
            bypass_cache=True
        )
        
        # Verify prompt sent to model was anonymized
        called_args, called_kwargs = mock_chat.call_args
        messages_sent = called_kwargs['messages']
        self.assertEqual(messages_sent[-1]['content'], "Hello [STAFF_1]")
        
        # Verify returned response is unmasked
        self.assertEqual(response, "Sure, I can help Alice Smith with their request.")

    def test_unmask_text_bare_tokens(self):
        """Regression: LLMs sometimes strip brackets, emitting STAFF_1 instead of [STAFF_1]."""
        from core.ai_utils import _unmask_text
        mapping = {
            "[STAFF_1]": "Bronwyn Driver",
            "[STAFF_2]": "James Martin",
            "[EMAIL_1]": "b.driver@nhs.net",
        }
        # Mixed: one bracketed, one bare, one email bare
        text = "Good morning, I've prepared a summary for STAFF_1. Today you will meet [STAFF_2]. Contact EMAIL_1 for details."
        result = _unmask_text(text, mapping)
        self.assertNotIn("STAFF_1", result)
        self.assertNotIn("STAFF_2", result)
        self.assertNotIn("EMAIL_1", result)
        self.assertIn("Bronwyn Driver", result)
        self.assertIn("James Martin", result)
        self.assertIn("b.driver@nhs.net", result)

    def test_unmask_text_all_brackets_intact(self):
        """When the LLM preserves brackets, _unmask_text should still work correctly."""
        from core.ai_utils import _unmask_text
        mapping = {"[STAFF_1]": "Alice Smith"}
        text = "Hello [STAFF_1], welcome."
        result = _unmask_text(text, mapping)
        self.assertEqual(result, "Hello Alice Smith, welcome.")

    def test_unmask_stream_bare_tokens(self):
        """Regression: unmask_stream should handle unbracketed tokens in the stream."""
        stream_chunks = ["Hello ", "STAFF_1", ", your ", "mee", "ting with STAFF_2 is at 12:00."]
        mapping = {
            "[STAFF_1]": "Bronwyn Driver",
            "[STAFF_2]": "James Martin",
        }
        unmasked = list(unmask_stream(stream_chunks, mapping))
        result = "".join(unmasked)
        self.assertIn("Bronwyn Driver", result)
        self.assertIn("James Martin", result)
        self.assertNotIn("STAFF_1", result)
        self.assertNotIn("STAFF_2", result)

    @patch('core.ai_utils.is_privacy_masking_enabled')
    @patch('core.ai_utils.get_db_pii_names')
    @patch('ollama.chat')
    def test_generate_ai_response_brackets_stripped_by_llm(self, mock_chat, mock_get_names, mock_enabled):
        """Regression: LLM strips brackets from mask tokens — names should still be restored."""
        mock_enabled.return_value = True
        mock_get_names.return_value = ["Bronwyn Driver", "James Martin"]

        # Simulate LLM returning bare STAFF_ tokens (no brackets)
        mock_chat.return_value = {
            "message": {
                "content": "Good morning STAFF_1. Today you meet STAFF_2 at 12:00."
            }
        }

        response = generate_ai_response(
            prompt="Prepare a briefing for Bronwyn Driver who meets James Martin today.",
            bypass_cache=True
        )

        self.assertNotIn("STAFF_1", response)
        self.assertNotIn("STAFF_2", response)
        self.assertIn("Bronwyn Driver", response)
        self.assertIn("James Martin", response)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# tests/test_career_planner.py
import unittest
from datetime import datetime
from core.database_utils import (

class TestCareerPlannerSchema(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # Initialise database and apply migrations
        init_database()
        
        # Add rating column self-healing in test database
        try:
            execute("SELECT rating FROM career_reflections LIMIT 1")
        except Exception:
            try:
                execute("ALTER TABLE career_reflections ADD COLUMN rating INTEGER DEFAULT 0")
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        # Clean state for test user ID 9999
        execute("DELETE FROM career_reflections WHERE user_id = 9999")
        execute("DELETE FROM career_vision WHERE user_id = 9999")
        execute("DELETE FROM career_factors WHERE user_id = 9999")
        
        # Clean goals, tactics, and notes linked to user 9999
        goals = fetch_all("SELECT id FROM career_goals WHERE user_id = 9999")
        for g_id in [g[0] for g in goals]:
            execute("DELETE FROM career_goal_tactics WHERE goal_id = ?", (g_id,))
            execute("DELETE FROM career_goal_notes WHERE goal_id = ?", (g_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM career_goals WHERE user_id = 9999")

    def test_tables_creation(self):
        """Verify that career planner tables exist in the database."""
        tables = ["career_reflections", "career_vision", "career_factors", "career_goals", "career_goal_tactics", "career_goal_notes"]
        for table in tables:
            row = fetch_one(f"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='{table}'")
            self.assertIsNotNone(row, f"Table '{table}' does not exist in SQLite schema")

    def test_career_reflections_operations(self):

            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)

                "Felt rushed near the deadline", "Underestimated the documentation scope", 
                "Improved time management skills", "Plan documentation incrementally in the future", 3
            )
        )

        self.assertIsNotNone(row)

        self.assertEqual(row[1], "Dedicated effort and pair programming")
        self.assertEqual(row[2], 3)

            WHERE user_id = 9999 AND is_deleted = 0

                "Updated felt rushed", "Updated underestimated scope",
                "Updated skills", "Updated incremental planning"
            )
        )
        
        # Verify updated values
        row_updated = fetch_one("SELECT pleased_with, rating, reflection_date FROM career_reflections WHERE user_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", (9999,))

        self.assertEqual(row_updated[1], 4)
        self.assertEqual(row_updated[2], "2026-07-16")

        # Soft Delete reflection
        execute("UPDATE career_reflections SET is_deleted = 1 WHERE user_id = 9999")

            INSERT INTO career_goals (
                user_id, title, description, timescale, specificity, complexity, 
                why_vision, what_strategy, status, created_at

                "Short-term (1-2 years)", "Specific", "Medium", 
                "Expands service engineering skills", "Follow Go tour and build 3 backend services", 
                "2026-07-15 12:00:00"
            )
        )

        # Get goal ID
        goal_row = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM career_goals WHERE user_id = 9999")
        self.assertIsNotNone(goal_row)
        goal_id = goal_row[0]

        # Insert tactics
        execute("INSERT INTO career_goal_tactics (goal_id, tactic_description, is_completed) VALUES (?, ?, 0)", (goal_id, "Complete Tour of Go"))
        execute("INSERT INTO career_goal_tactics (goal_id, tactic_description, is_completed) VALUES (?, ?, 0)", (goal_id, "Write a CLI tool in Go"))

        # Verify tactics
        tactics = fetch_all("SELECT id, tactic_description, is_completed FROM career_goal_tactics WHERE goal_id = ?", (goal_id,))
        self.assertEqual(len(tactics), 2)
        self.assertEqual(tactics[0][1], "Complete Tour of Go")

        # Toggle tactic completion
        tactic_id = tactics[0][0]
        execute("UPDATE career_goal_tactics SET is_completed = 1 WHERE id = ?", (tactic_id,))
        t_status = fetch_one("SELECT is_completed FROM career_goal_tactics WHERE id = ?", (tactic_id,))
        self.assertEqual(t_status[0], 1)

        # Verify cascade delete
        execute("DELETE FROM career_goals WHERE id = ?", (goal_id,))
        t_count = fetch_one("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM career_goal_tactics WHERE goal_id = ?", (goal_id,))
        self.assertEqual(t_count[0], 0)

    def test_career_goal_notes_operations(self):
        """Verify note creation, listing, soft deletion and cascade on goal delete."""
        # Insert goal first
        execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO career_goals (
                user_id, title, description, timescale, specificity, complexity, 
                why_vision, what_strategy, status, created_at
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'Active', ?)
            """,
            (
                9999, "Go Programming", "Learn Go",
                "Short-term (1-2 years)", "Specific", "Medium", 
                "Expands skills", "Follow Go tour", 
                "2026-07-15 12:00:00"
            )
        )
        goal_id = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM career_goals WHERE user_id = 9999")[0]

        # Insert note
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO career_goal_notes (goal_id, note_text, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (goal_id, "Completed initial module research.", "2026-07-16 12:00:00")
        )

        # Verify note exists
        note_row = fetch_one("SELECT note_text, created_at FROM career_goal_notes WHERE goal_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", (goal_id,))
        self.assertIsNotNone(note_row)
        self.assertEqual(note_row[0], "Completed initial module research.")
        self.assertEqual(note_row[1], "2026-07-16 12:00:00")

        # Soft delete note
        note_id = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM career_goal_notes WHERE goal_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", (goal_id,))[0]
        execute("UPDATE career_goal_notes SET is_deleted = 1 WHERE id = ?", (note_id,))
        note_del_row = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM career_goal_notes WHERE goal_id = ? AND is_deleted = 0", (goal_id,))
        self.assertIsNone(note_del_row)

        # Reactivate note to test cascade deletion when goal is deleted
        execute("UPDATE career_goal_notes SET is_deleted = 0 WHERE id = ?", (note_id,))
        
        # Delete goal
        execute("DELETE FROM career_goals WHERE id = ?", (goal_id,))
        notes_count = fetch_one("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM career_goal_notes WHERE goal_id = ?", (goal_id,))[0]
        self.assertEqual(notes_count, 0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# tests/test_milestone_trends.py
import unittest
import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from core.database_utils import query, execute, fetch_one, get_milestone_trends

class TestMilestoneTrends(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # Set up a mock org and project
        execute("INSERT INTO orgs (name) VALUES ('Test Org Milestone')")
        self.org_id = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM orgs WHERE name = 'Test Org Milestone'")[0]
        
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO projects (org_id, name, status, start_date, due_date) 
            VALUES (?, 'Test Project Milestone', 'Testing', ?, ?)
        """, (self.org_id, "2026-04-01", "2026-07-01"))
        self.project_id = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM projects WHERE name = 'Test Project Milestone'")[0]
        
        # Add some system-wide snapshots to verify query works
        execute("INSERT INTO snapshots (date, phase, count) VALUES ('2026-04-01', 'Discovery', 5)")
        self.snapshot_id = fetch_one("SELECT id FROM snapshots WHERE date = '2026-04-01'")[0]

    def tearDown(self):
        # Clean up mock data
        execute("DELETE FROM project_milestones WHERE project_id = ?", (self.project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM phase_history WHERE project_id = ?", (self.project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?", (self.project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM orgs WHERE id = ?", (self.org_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM snapshots WHERE id = ?", (self.snapshot_id,))

    def test_achieved_milestone_trends(self):
        # Milestone 1: Achieved on time
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, actual_date, status, trend)
            VALUES (?, 'M1', '2026-04-10', '2026-04-10', 'Achieved', 'Stable')
        """, (self.project_id,))
        
        # Milestone 2: Achieved early
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, actual_date, status, trend)
            VALUES (?, 'M2', '2026-04-15', '2026-04-12', 'Achieved', 'Stable')
        """, (self.project_id,))
        
        # Milestone 3: Achieved late
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, actual_date, status, trend)
            VALUES (?, 'M3', '2026-04-20', '2026-04-25', 'Achieved', 'Stable')
        """, (self.project_id,))
        
        df = get_milestone_trends(self.project_id)
        
        m1 = df[df['name'] == 'M1'].iloc[0]
        m2 = df[df['name'] == 'M2'].iloc[0]
        m3 = df[df['name'] == 'M3'].iloc[0]
        
        self.assertEqual(m1['trend'], 'Stable')
        self.assertEqual(m2['trend'], 'Accelerating')
        self.assertEqual(m3['trend'], 'Slipping')

    def test_incomplete_past_milestone_trend(self):
        # Milestone in the past but not achieved
        past_date = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=5)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, status, trend)
            VALUES (?, 'Past Incomplete', ?, 'Planned', 'Stable')
        """, (self.project_id, past_date))
        
        df = get_milestone_trends(self.project_id)
        m = df[df['name'] == 'Past Incomplete'].iloc[0]
        self.assertEqual(m['trend'], 'Slipping')

    def test_future_milestone_project_trends(self):
        # Future milestone, should look at project phase progress.
        # Let's mock phase history:
        # Phase order: Discovery, Mapping, Testing
        # Baseline durations: Discovery=20, Mapping=30, Testing=30 (Total 80)
        # 1. Discovery started 2026-04-01, ended 2026-04-10 (took 9 days, baseline 20: accelerated)
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO phase_history (project_id, phase, start_date, end_date)
            VALUES (?, 'Discovery', '2026-04-01', '2026-04-10')
        """, (self.project_id,))
        
        # 2. Mapping started 2026-04-10, ended 2026-04-20 (took 10 days, baseline 30: accelerated)
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO phase_history (project_id, phase, start_date, end_date)
            VALUES (?, 'Mapping', '2026-04-10', '2026-04-20')
        """, (self.project_id,))
        
        # 3. Testing started 2026-04-20, still ongoing.
        # Let's say today is 2026-04-25 (only 5 days into Testing, baseline 30).
        # Cumulative actual so far is 9 + 10 + 5 = 24 days.
        # Cumulative baseline is 20 + 30 + 30 = 80 days.
        # Since actual (24) < baseline (80) - 5, project is accelerating!
        
        # To simulate this, we can set start_date of Testing phase to be very recent.
        today_str = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        yesterday_str = (datetime.now() - timedelta(days=1)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO phase_history (project_id, phase, start_date, end_date)
            VALUES (?, 'Testing', ?, NULL)
        """, (self.project_id, yesterday_str))
        
        future_date = (datetime.now() + timedelta(days=10)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        execute("""
            INSERT INTO project_milestones (project_id, name, planned_date, status, trend)
            VALUES (?, 'Future Milestone', ?, 'Planned', 'Stable')
        """, (self.project_id, future_date))
        
        df = get_milestone_trends(self.project_id)
        m = df[df['name'] == 'Future Milestone'].iloc[0]
        # In this scenario, it should calculate it as 'Accelerating'
        self.assertEqual(m['trend'], 'Accelerating')

    def test_compute_ideal_baseline(self):
        from core.logic import compute_ideal_baseline
        import pandas as pd
        start_date = datetime(2026, 4, 1).date()
        end_date = datetime(2026, 4, 11).date() # 10 days duration
        total_tasks = 10
        
        date_range = pd.date_range(start="2026-03-31", end="2026-04-12") # 13 days
        
        baseline = compute_ideal_baseline(total_tasks, start_date, end_date, date_range)
        
        # date_range[0] is 2026-03-31 (before start_date)
        self.assertEqual(baseline[0], 10.0)
        
        # date_range[1] is 2026-04-01 (start_date) -> 10 tasks
        self.assertEqual(baseline[1], 10.0)
        
        # date_range[6] is 2026-04-06 (midpoint) -> 5.0 tasks
        self.assertEqual(baseline[6], 5.0)
        
        # date_range[11] is 2026-04-11 (end_date) -> 0 tasks
        self.assertEqual(baseline[11], 0.0)
        
        # date_range[12] is 2026-04-12 (after end_date) -> 0 tasks
        self.assertEqual(baseline[12], 0.0)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# tests/test_ai_cache_coalescing.py
import unittest
import sys
import time
import threading
import sqlite3
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

# Save original modules before mocking
_original_modules = {}
for m in ['streamlit', 'chromadb', 'core.database_utils']:
    if m in sys.modules:
        _original_modules[m] = sys.modules[m]

# 1. Mock dependencies before importing core.ai_utils
mock_streamlit = MagicMock()
mock_streamlit.runtime.exists.return_value = False
mock_streamlit.session_state = {}
sys.modules['streamlit'] = mock_streamlit

mock_chromadb = MagicMock()
sys.modules['chromadb'] = mock_chromadb

# Set up in-memory database for testing cache operations
test_conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", check_same_thread=False)
cursor = test_conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ai_response_cache (
        prompt_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        response TEXT,
        model_name TEXT,
        temperature REAL,
        created_at TEXT,
        prompt TEXT,
        system_prompt TEXT
    )
""")
cursor.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_config (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        category TEXT NOT NULL,
        value TEXT NOT NULL
    )
""")
cursor.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO app_config (category, value) VALUES ('AI_MODEL_NAME', 'llama3:8b')")
cursor.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO app_config (category, value) VALUES ('SMALL_AI_MODEL_NAME', 'phi3:latest')")
test_conn.commit()

db_lock = threading.Lock()

def mock_fetch_one(sql, params=None):
    with db_lock:
        c = test_conn.cursor()
        c.execute(sql, params or ())
        return c.fetchone()

def mock_execute_silent(sql, params=None, return_lastrowid=False):
    with db_lock:
        c = test_conn.cursor()
        c.execute(sql, params or ())
        test_conn.commit()
        return c.lastrowid

mock_database_utils = MagicMock()
mock_database_utils.fetch_one = mock_fetch_one
mock_database_utils.execute_silent = mock_execute_silent
mock_database_utils.query = MagicMock()
mock_database_utils.get_connection = MagicMock()
sys.modules['core.database_utils'] = mock_database_utils

# Import core.ai_utils now that mocks are in place
import core.ai_utils
from core.ai_utils import generate_ai_response

class TestAiCacheCoalescing(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # Clear database cache table before each test (but keep app_config seeded)
        with db_lock:
            cursor.execute("DELETE FROM ai_response_cache")
            test_conn.commit()

    @patch('core.ai_utils.ollama.chat')
    def test_sequential_caching(self, mock_chat):
        # Set up mock Ollama response
        mock_chat.return_value = {
            'message': {'content': 'This is a test response.'}
        }

        # First call: should query Ollama and save to cache
        response1 = generate_ai_response(
            prompt="Write a test prompt",
            system_prompt="Test System Prompt",
            temperature=0.0
        )
        self.assertEqual(response1, 'This is a test response.')
        self.assertEqual(mock_chat.call_count, 1)

        # Second call: should hit cache and skip Ollama
        response2 = generate_ai_response(
            prompt="Write a test prompt",
            system_prompt="Test System Prompt",
            temperature=0.0
        )
        self.assertEqual(response2, 'This is a test response.')
        self.assertEqual(mock_chat.call_count, 1)  # Call count remains 1

    @patch('core.ai_utils.ollama.chat')
    def test_concurrent_coalescing(self, mock_chat):
        call_count = 0
        call_lock = threading.Lock()

        def slow_chat(model, messages, options=None):
            nonlocal call_count
            with call_lock:
                call_count += 1
            # Simulate network latency/inference time
            time.sleep(0.3)
            return {
                'message': {'content': f'Response for {messages[-1]["content"]}'}
            }

        mock_chat.side_effect = slow_chat

        results = []
        threads = []

        def worker():
            res = generate_ai_response(
                prompt="Coalesced Prompt",
                system_prompt="Coalesced System Prompt",
                temperature=0.0
            )
            results.append(res)

        # Launch 3 threads concurrently
        for _ in range(3):
            t = threading.Thread(target=worker)
            threads.append(t)
            t.start()

        # Wait for all threads to complete
        for t in threads:
            t.join()

        # Assertions
        # 1. Ollama chat should have been called exactly once
        self.assertEqual(call_count, 1)
        # 2. All 3 threads should have received the identical correct response
        self.assertEqual(len(results), 3)
        for r in results:
            self.assertEqual(r, "Response for Coalesced Prompt")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

def tearDownModule():
    for m in ['streamlit', 'chromadb', 'core.database_utils']:
        if m in _original_modules:
            sys.modules[m] = _original_modules[m]
        else:
            sys.modules.pop(m, None)

# tests/test_pre_migration_profiling.py
import unittest
import pandas as pd
import json
import io
from core.database_utils import execute, query, profile_migration_data

class TestPreMigrationProfiling(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # 1. Create a dummy organisation
        self.org_id = execute(
            "INSERT INTO orgs (name, region) VALUES ('Test Profiling Org', 'London')", 
            return_lastrowid=True
        )
        # 2. Create a dummy project
        self.project_id = execute(
            "INSERT INTO projects (org_id, name, status, is_deleted) VALUES (?, 'Test Profiling Project', 'Active', 0)", 
            (self.org_id,), 
            return_lastrowid=True
        )

    def tearDown(self):
        # Clean up database tables
        execute("DELETE FROM data_validation_rules WHERE project_id = ?", (self.project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM data_cleanse_rules WHERE project_id = ?", (self.project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?", (self.project_id,))
        execute("DELETE FROM orgs WHERE id = ?", (self.org_id,))

    def test_default_profile(self):
        # Test profiling with default mock dataset (no rules seeded)
        result = profile_migration_data(self.project_id)
        
        self.assertIn("total_records", result)
        self.assertEqual(result["total_records"], 6)
        self.assertEqual(result["cleansing_rules_applied"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["validation_rules_checked"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["health_score"], 100.0)
        self.assertIn("missing_fields", result)
        self.assertIn("email_validation", result)
        self.assertIn("hierarchy_validation", result)

    def test_cleansing_rules(self):
        # Seed cleansing rules for the project
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_cleanse_rules (project_id, rule_name, target_column, transformation_type, parameters) VALUES (?, 'Upper Job Title', 'Job_Title', 'Uppercase', '{}')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_cleanse_rules (project_id, rule_name, target_column, transformation_type, parameters) VALUES (?, 'Fill Department', 'Department', 'Fill Nulls', '{\"fill_value\": \"General\"}')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_cleanse_rules (project_id, rule_name, target_column, transformation_type, parameters) VALUES (?, 'Replace Band', 'Pay_Band', 'Replace', '{\"find\": \"Band \", \"replace\": \"Grade \"}')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        
        # Custom input dataframe
        csv_data = """Staff_ID,Name,Job_Title,Email,Department,Pay_Band
1001,John Doe,specialist nurse,j.doe@nhs.net,,Band 5
1002,Jane Smith,Clinical Director,j.smith@nhs.net,Clinical,Band 8b
"""
        df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
        
        result = profile_migration_data(self.project_id, df=df)
        
        # Verify rules applied count
        self.assertEqual(result["cleansing_rules_applied"], 3)
        
        # Verify categorical distributions reflect cleaned values
        val_dists = result["value_distributions"]
        
        # "specialist nurse" -> "SPECIALIST NURSE"
        self.assertIn("SPECIALIST NURSE", val_dists.get("Job_Title", {}))
        
        # Empty department filled with "General"
        self.assertEqual(val_dists.get("Department", {}).get("General"), 1)
        
        # "Band 5" -> "Grade 5"
        self.assertIn("Grade 5", val_dists.get("Pay_Band", {}))

    def test_validation_rules(self):
        # Seed validation rules
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_validation_rules (project_id, column_name, rule_type, rule_value) VALUES (?, 'Staff_ID', 'is_unique', '')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_validation_rules (project_id, column_name, rule_type, rule_value) VALUES (?, 'Name', 'not_empty', '')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_validation_rules (project_id, column_name, rule_type, rule_value) VALUES (?, 'ODS_Code', 'ods_code', '')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        execute(
            "INSERT INTO data_validation_rules (project_id, column_name, rule_type, rule_value) VALUES (?, 'Pay_Band', 'afc_band', '')",
            (self.project_id,)
        )
        
        # Input with violations
        csv_data = """Staff_ID,Name,ODS_Code,Pay_Band
1001,John Doe,RXR,Band 5
1001,Jane Smith,INVALID_ODS,Band 12
1003,,RTD,Band 8a
"""
        df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
        
        result = profile_migration_data(self.project_id, df=df)
        
        # 3 rows, 4 rules = 12 total checks
        # Failures: 1 duplicate Staff_ID, 1 empty Name, 1 invalid ODS_Code, 1 invalid Pay_Band = 4 failures
        # Passed checks = 12 - 4 = 8
        # Health score = 8 / 12 * 100 = 66.7%
        self.assertEqual(result["validation_rules_checked"], 4)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(result["health_score"], 66.7, places=1)
        
        # Verify warnings list populated
        warning_types = [w["type"] for w in result["warnings"]]
        self.assertIn("Uniqueness Conflict", warning_types)
        self.assertIn("Data Completeness Alert", warning_types)
        self.assertIn("ODS Code Invalid", warning_types)
        self.assertIn("AfC Band Invalid", warning_types)

    def test_email_validation(self):
        csv_data = """Staff_ID,Name,Email
1001,John Doe,j.doe@nhs.net
1002,Jane Smith,invalid_email_format
1003,Bob Johnson,bob@company
"""
        df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
        
        result = profile_migration_data(self.project_id, df=df)
        
        email_val = result["email_validation"]
        self.assertEqual(email_val["failures_count"], 2)
        failures_staff_ids = [f["staff_id"] for f in email_val["failures"]]
        self.assertIn("1002", failures_staff_ids)
        self.assertIn("1003", failures_staff_ids)

    def test_hierarchy_validation(self):
        # 1001 reports to 1002
        # 1002 reports to 1003
        # 1003 reports to 1001 (circular: 1001 -> 1002 -> 1003 -> 1001)
        # 1004 has missing manager link
        # 1005 reports to non-existent ID 9999
        # 1006 reports to themselves (1006)
        csv_data = """Staff_ID,Name,Line_Manager_ID
1001,Emp A,1002
1002,Emp B,1003
1003,Emp C,1001
1004,Emp D,
1005,Emp E,9999
1006,Emp F,1006
"""
        df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))
        
        result = profile_migration_data(self.project_id, df=df)
        
        h_val = result["hierarchy_validation"]
        
        # Verify counts
        self.assertEqual(h_val["missing_manager_links"], 1) # Emp D
        self.assertEqual(h_val["invalid_manager_ids"], 2) # Emp E (9999), Emp F (1006 self)
        self.assertEqual(h_val["circular_links"], 3) # Emp A, Emp B, Emp C
        
        # Verify details
        details = h_val["details"]
        self.assertEqual(len(details), 6)
        
        error_types = [d["error_type"] for d in details]
        self.assertIn("Missing Manager", error_types)
        self.assertIn("Manager Not Found", error_types)
        self.assertIn("Self Reference", error_types)
        self.assertIn("Circular Reference", error_types)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
